brief_summary:
The goal of this interventional study is to evaluate the SKIN CARE nursing bundle for the prevention of medical device-related pressure injuries (MDRPIs) among critically ill adult patients admitted to surgical intensive care units (ICUs). The study also aims to examine changes in patients' pressure injury risk over the ICU stay.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does implementation of the SKIN CARE bundle reduce the occurrence of medical device-related pressure injuries compared with routine intensive care?
* Does implementation of the SKIN CARE bundle reduce the occurrence of medical device-related mucosal membrane pressure injuries?
* Does the SKIN CARE bundle improve patients' pressure injury risk profiles, as measured by the Braden Scale, during their ICU stay? Researchers compared patients receiving routine intensive care with patients receiving the SKIN CARE bundle to evaluate differences in medical device-related pressure injuries, including mucosal membrane and staged skin pressure injuries, as well as changes in Braden Scale scores over time.

Participants were 130 critically ill adult patients admitted to three surgical intensive care units at a governmental hospital in Mansoura, Egypt. They were allocated sequentially into two groups:

* Control group (65 participants): Received routine intensive care, including general skin assessment, repositioning according to clinical needs, skin hygiene, pressure-redistribution measures when indicated, nutritional support, and routine medical device securement.
* Intervention group (65 participants): Received intensive care incorporating the SKIN CARE nursing bundle, consisting of eight components:

  * Secure medical devices appropriately and use protective dressings when indicated.
  * Keep repositioning medical devices regularly when clinically feasible and remove unnecessary devices.
  * Inspect the skin beneath and around medical devices at least twice daily.
  * Nutrition and hydration assessment.
  * Choose appropriate medical device types and sizes.
  * Avoid placing medical devices over existing pressure injuries when clinically feasible.
  * Report and document identified medical device-related pressure injuries promptly.
  * Educate nursing staff about medical device-related pressure injury prevention. All participants underwent baseline assessment and daily follow-up. The Braden Scale was used to assess pressure injury risk, and a medical device-related pressure injury assessment checklist was used to identify and classify injuries. Follow-up continued until ICU discharge or completion of the 12-day observation period, whichever occurred first.
primary_outcomes: Occurrence of Medical Device-Related Pressure Injuries (MDRPIs)
title: Nurse-Led SKIN CARE Bundle on Medical Device-Related Pressure Injuries

brief_summary:
Over 12,000 women in Ontario will be diagnosed with BC this year. The COVID-19 pandemic changed the healthcare system, making it important to have high-quality virtual (online) care. Mobile health, which means getting health services on your phone, has become a common part of healthcare.

A previously developed app will be used in this study to improve the virtual care experience for BC patients that will be undergoing neoadjuvant chemotherapy. With this app, patients can:

* Get personalized resources that can help them navigate through the stages of their treatment.
* Access vetted information about their cancer \& treatment from a health library.
* Receive surveys about their health and well-being.
* Get mental and social support from an e-coach, who are volunteers trained to help and support patients. The e-coaches will provide information, listen to how participants are feeling, and help participants find information they might need.
* Connect with a physiotherapist to discuss healthy living and wellness.

Participants will be randomly put into one of two groups: one group will use the app, while the other will continue to get usual care without the app. Participants will have access to the app for 12 months. They will be asked about their experience, how they are feeling, and their health status at several timepoints.

At the end of the study, the two groups will be compared to see how active and engaged participants are in their treatment and see how this changes over 12 months. The study team will also examine how participants are feeling emotionally and their overall quality of life. Health service utilization data and chart review will be used to examine how patients used health services over the course of their treatment. Qualitative interviews will be conducted for some patients about their treatment and experience on the app, using photos that they submit throughout the study.
title: The ABODE Study for Patients Undergoing Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy

brief_summary: This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter phase II clinical trial. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of SAL0167, an oral PCSK9 inhibitor, in lowering low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in participants with hyperlipidemia. Participants will be randomized 1:1:1:1 to receive low-dose SAL0167, medium-dose SAL0167, high-dose SAL0167, or placebo for a treatment period of 8 weeks.
primary_outcomes: Percent Change From Baseline in Low-density Lipoprotein Cholesterol (LDL-C)
title: Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of SAL0167 Tablets at Different Doses in Participants With Hyperlipidemia.

brief_summary: This study compares four educational methods for teaching thyroid ultrasound interpretation to novice learners. Preclinical medical students with no prior training in thyroid ultrasound or the Korean Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (K-TIRADS) are randomly assigned to one of four groups: (A) traditional one-on-one apprenticeship training, (B) self-learning with images labeled only as benign or malignant, (C) self-learning assisted by an artificial intelligence-based computer-aided diagnosis (AI-CAD) system, or (D) self-learning with images structured by K-TIRADS category. The study aims to determine which method most effectively improves diagnostic performance (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and agreement with expert K-TIRADS assessment), how quickly learners reach a target level of proficiency, whether AI-CAD provides additional educational value for novices, and how each method affects user cognitive load.
primary_outcomes: Change in diagnostic accuracy for benign versus malignant thyroid nodules
Change in sensitivity for malignant thyroid nodules
Change in specificity for malignant thyroid nodules
Change in agreement with expert K-TIRADS assessment (ultrasound lexicon and final category)
title: Educational Methods for Learning Thyroid Ultrasound Interpretation in Medical Students

brief_summary:
This is a decentralized, observational pilot study evaluating the potential effects of Snap Supplements Prostate Health on urinary symptoms in men aged 50 years and older. Prostate enlargement and related urinary issues, such as daytime frequency, nighttime urination (nocturia), and urgency, are common with age and may negatively affect quality of life and sleep.

In this study, approximately 50 participants will take three capsules of Snap Supplements Prostate Health nightly for 90 days while completing brief daily surveys using a secure online platform (Alethios). Surveys will track urinary frequency, nocturia, urgency, and sleep quality, with additional questions about product tolerability, satisfaction, and overall experience.

The main goal is to explore whether taking the supplement for 90 days is associated with improvement in urinary symptoms compared with each participant's own baseline. This is a single-group, pre-post study without randomization or placebo. No in-person visits are required; all activities occur at home.

The supplement contains a blend of natural ingredients (such as saw palmetto, beta-sitosterol, nettle root, turmeric, green tea extract, and mushroom extracts) that have been studied for their potential effects on prostate and urinary health. The study will help characterize user experiences in a real-world setting and generate preliminary data to inform future research.

Participation is voluntary, and participants may withdraw at any time. Compensation is provided for completing surveys. Risks are expected to be minimal, with possible mild gastrointestinal or allergic-type reactions.
title: Pilot Study on the Effects of Snap Supplements Prostate Health Formula on Urinary Symptoms in Men Over 50

brief_summary:
Infraorbital hollowing, also known as tear trough deformity, refers to a sunken groove extending from the medial canthal region along the infraorbital rim downward and laterally. It is one of the key features of facial aging and remains one of the most challenging issues in periorbital rejuvenation \[1,2\]. This deformity is particularly common among Asian populations, with approximately 60%-70% of middle-aged individuals presenting with varying degrees of infraorbital hollowing \[2\]; its incidence increases significantly with age. The formation of infraorbital hollowing results from the combined effects of multiple factors, including anatomical changes, soft tissue atrophy, skin aging, and impaired lymphatic circulation \[2\]. Beyond compromising facial aesthetics, it creates negative impressions of fatigue, aging, and sternness, which can severely affect patients' psychological well-being and social lives \[3\]. In recent years, driven by growing demand for facial rejuvenation, infraorbital hollowing correction has become a popular non-surgical aesthetic procedure.

However, due to the complex anatomy of the infraorbital region-characterized by thin skin, abundant vasculature, and fragile lymphatic drainage-traditional fillers are prone to issues such as migration, the Tyndall effect, and prolonged swelling, placing higher demands on both filling materials and injection techniques \[4\]. Collagen, as a natural biomaterial, offers distinct advantages for infraorbital hollowing correction owing to its excellent biocompatibility, low migration tendency, and light-scattering properties \[5\]. The mechanism of collagen injection for infraorbital hollowing correction is a complex, multi-stage, and multi-level process that achieves immediate physical volumization and tissue support. Injected collagen replenishes lost volume, forming a soft, cohesive fibrous structure that lifts the depressed area and restores a smooth transition between the lower eyelid and cheek, thereby reducing the hollowed appearance \[5,6\]. Meanwhile, due to its high adhesiveness, collagen binds loosened skin tissues together, repositions the disrupted fibrous scaffold network, and restores a youthful, firm contour \[6\]. After injection, the collagen gradually dehydrates and condenses, reorganizing into a fibrillar structure resembling native collagen in vivo, which further tightens tissues and enhances the supporting effect.

The medical collagen filler developed by Feifan (Changchun) Medical Biotechnology Co., Ltd. was approved for marketing by the NMPA in 2016 (Registration Certificate No.: Guo Xie Zhu Zhun 20163131609). It is indicated for dermal filling of the face to correct moderate to severe nasolabial folds, and has demonstrated favorable efficacy and safety in clinical practice. The proposed new indication is infraorbital filling for the improvement and correction of infraorbital hollowing. The objective of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of this medical collagen filler manufactured by Feifan (Changchun) Medical Biotechnology Co., Ltd. in correcting the severity of infraorbital hollowing. In accordance with the Measures for the Administration of Medical Device Registration and Filing, the Good Clinical Practice for Medical Device Clinical Trials (GCP), and the Guidelines for Medical Device Clinical Trial Design, and adhering to the ethical principles of the World Medical Association Declaration of Helsinki, this study strives to maximize benefits for research participants while minimizing potential harm.
primary_outcomes: The effective rate of improvement in AIHS (Assessment of Infraorbital Hollowing Severity) scores
title: A Prospective, Multicenter, Randomized, No-Treatment Controlled, Evaluator-Blinded, Superiority Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of a Medical Collagen Filler for Correcting Infraorbital Depression

brief_summary: Sarcopenic obesity (SO) in older adults involves the co-occurrence of skeletal muscle decline and excessive body fat. This project investigates the gut-muscle axis, specifically how gut bacteria convert dietary polyphenols (such as ellagic acid found in pomegranates) into a muscle-protecting metabolite called Urolithin A (UA). This study is a randomized crossover pilot trial in 30 older adults with SO. It tests whether combining a pomegranate extract supplement with a prebiotic (Fructo-oligosaccharides, or FOS) increases the body's production of UA more effectively than pomegranate extract alone over a 7-day period.
title: Pomegranate-Prebiotic Supplementation for Sarcopenic Obesity

brief_summary: The aim of this prospective, observational, non-interventional study is to evaluate the level of agreement between IEO-MATCH, a newly developed AI-based clinical trial matcher, and the standard manual matching workflow in assigning patients to phase I clinical trials open at IEO in the Division of New Drugs and Early Drug Development.
interventions: The study is observational and non-interventional.
primary_outcomes: Concordance between standard and automatic matching
title: Smart Artificial Intelligence for Trial Linking

brief_summary:
The primary objective of this split-mouth clinical trial is to evaluate the clinical efficacy of topical Blue M gel compared to a conventional periodontal dressing (Coe-Pak) following gingivectomy.

Each participant will receive both treatments on opposite sides of the dental arch, with Blue M gel consistently applied to the right side and Coe-Pak to the left side.

The study aims to assess post-operative outcomes using three main clinical parameters: patient-reported pain levels via the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), wound healing using Landry's Healing Index, and gingival inflammation using the Gingival Index (GI).

These parameters will be evaluated at specific follow-up intervals up to 28 days post-surgery.
title: Effect of Blue M Gel on Healing After Gingivectomy

brief_summary:
This is a phase 1, randomized, open-label, single-center, single-dose, three-period, six-sequence crossover study in healthy adult volunteers. The study is designed to compare the relative bioavailability of itraconazole tablet (T26, Test) with itraconazole capsule (Sporanox®, Reference) under fed conditions; and to assess the food effect from a high-fat meal on T26.

Three treatments, as described below, are planned:

Test Product (Tfed): T26, 130 mg (two 65 mg tablets), administered under fed conditions Reference Product (R): Sporanox®, 200 mg (two 100 mg capsules), administered under fed conditions Test Product (Tfasted): T26, 130 mg (two 65 mg tablets), administered under fasted conditions A total of 18 participants will be randomized 1:1:1:1:1:1 into six different treatment sequences (TfastTfedR, TfastRTfed, TfedTfastR, TfedRTfast, RTfastTfed, RTfedTfast). The dosing between two consecutive treatment periods will be separated by a minimum 14-day washout interval.

This study consists of three periods: a screening period (Day -7\~Day -2), a cross-over treatment period, and a safety follow-up visit (Day 36 \~Day 43). During each treatment period, eligible participants will be admitted to the clinical research unit (CRU) one day prior to dosing and will receive a single oral dose of the assigned study treatment on Day 1 according to the randomized sequence. On Day 1 of each treatment period, T26 or Sporanox® will be administered with 240 mL of water at approximately 8:00 a.m. (±1 hour) under fasted or fed condition. Detailed dietary requirements and dosing procedures. Participants will discharge from the CRU on the fifth day of each treatment period after completion of the scheduled safety assessments and collection of the last PK blood sample (up to 96 hours post-dose).
title: A Phase 1, Randomized, Open-Label, Single-Center, Single-Dose, Three-Period, Six-Sequence Crossover Study in Healthy Volunteers to Compare the Relative Bioavailability of Itraconazole Tablet (T26) and Itraconazole Capsule (Sporanox®) Under Fed Conditions and to Assess the Food Effect on T26

brief_summary:
This study aims to examine the effect of nursing care based on the salutogenesis model on the sense of integrity and functionality levels in individuals with bipolar disorder. The scope of the study includes the evaluation of the effects of model-based care initiatives applied to individuals diagnosed with bipolar disorder on individuals' psychosocial adaptation, stress coping capacity and daily life functionality.

The study focuses on preventive and developmental care approaches in the field of mental health and disease nursing. The research is experimental in nature and will be carried out in an intervention and control group design. Within the scope of the study, structured nursing care based on the salutogenesis model will be applied to the intervention group, while routine care will be provided to the control group. The data will be collected through the sociodemographic information form, the sense of integrity scale and valid and reliable scales that measure the level of functionality in bipolar disorder. By comparing the pre-test and post-test measurements, the effect of the maintenance model will be analyzed using statistical methods. The original value of the study is that nursing care based on the salutogenesis model was considered experimentally for the first time in individuals diagnosed with bipolar disorder. Although the use of this model in chronic diseases is limited in the literature, there are no studies aimed at its application in psychiatric diseases, especially bipolar disorder. In this aspect, the research offers a unique contribution in terms of integrating a theoretical model into clinical nursing practice.

As a result of the study, it is predicted that care based on the salutogenesis model strengthens the sense of integrity of individuals and increases their level of functionality. It is expected that the findings to be obtained will contribute to psychiatric nursing practices, the development of care plans and the improvement of the quality of mental health services, the increase of professional satisfaction of mental health workers and the prevention of burnout problems.
interventions: care based on the salutogenesis model
primary_outcomes: Change in Sense of Coherence Score
title: SALUTOGENESIS MODEL

brief_summary:
The convergence of evidence from neoCARHP (comparable pCR between TCHP and THP in an unselected population), DB-11 (activity of T-DXd-THP in high-risk HER2-positive early breast cancer), and I-SPY2 ctDNA data (early ctDNA clearance predicts favorable response and outcomes) provides a strong rationale for biomarker-guided treatment selection. This study uses early on-treatment ctDNA response after standardized THP induction to direct therapy intensity rather than reflexively escalating all patients.

Unlike non-biomarker-selected escalation approaches, this study uses ctDNA as a dynamic biomarker to tailor therapy: patients with early molecular clearance continue THP without carboplatin or ADC exposure, while patients with persistent molecular tumor burden escalate to T-DXd.
primary_outcomes: pCR rate in the HR-positive/HER2-positive group
pCR rate in the HR-negative/HER2-positive group
title: ctDNA-Guided Neoadjuvant Therapy in HER2+ Breast Cancer

brief_summary:
The goal of this pilot clinical trial is to learn whether paired associative stimulation (PAS) of the primary motor cortex and the cervical spinal dorsal roots, delivered through implanted epidural electrodes and combined with neurorehabilitation, is safe in adults with chronic paresis or paralysis of the arm and hand after a stroke in the territory of the middle cerebral artery.

The main question it aims to answer is:

\* What adverse events occur during 12 months of follow-up with this treatment?

Secondary questions are whether the stimulation is feasible (whether pairing the corresponding electrode contacts of the motor cortex and the cervical spinal cord increases the motor response to stimulation) and whether it shows preliminary signs of efficacy on upper limb motor function, quality of life and caregiver burden.

Researchers will compare PAS plus rehabilitation with sham stimulation plus rehabilitation during a two-month double-blind phase.

Participants will:

* Have epidural electrodes surgically implanted over the primary motor cortex and the cervical spinal cord, connected to an implanted pulse generator
* Receive PAS or sham stimulation together with rehabilitation sessions for two months
* If assigned to sham stimulation, receive open-label PAS plus rehabilitation for a further two months
* Attend follow-up visits for 12 months
interventions: Epidural paired associative stimulation of the motor cortex and cervical dorsal roots
title: Paired Associative Stimulation of the Motor Cortex and the Dorsal Roots of the Cervical Spine for the Recovery of Arm and Hand Function in Chronic Middle Cerebral Artery Stroke. ASCLEPIUS Safety Evaluation Pilot Study

brief_summary: The primary aim of the study is to explore the effectiveness of Berotralstat in preventing angioedema attacks in patients with Acquired Angioedema (AAE-C1-INH).
conditions: Acquired Angioedema Due to C1-Inhibitor Deficiency (AAE-C1-INH)

brief_summary: Esprit BTK Japan Post-Marketing Surveillance (PMS) is a database-based PMS. The purpose of this PMS is to confirm the safety and effectiveness of the Esprit BTK Everolimus Eluting Resorbable Scaffold System for the treatment of below-the-knee artery disease in the real-world clinical setting in Japan. The Surveillance will register all patients in whom treatment with Esprit BTK was attempted.
interventions: Esprit BTK Everolimus Eluting Resorbable Scaffold System

Freedom at 1 year from the composite of the following events

brief_summary:
Insomnia, anxiety, and depression are common mental health problems that frequently occur together. Psychological interventions that address shared processes underlying these symptoms may offer an accessible way to improve mental health and sleep.

This study will evaluate the effectiveness of Vínculo, an eight-week, guided digital psychological intervention for adults experiencing clinically significant symptoms of insomnia, anxiety, and/or depression.

Approximately 305 adults living in Brazil will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. The experimental group will receive Vínculo, a psychological intervention delivered through a WhatsApp chatbot that combines acceptance and commitment therapy, behavioral activation, and behavioral strategies for sleep. The comparison group will receive an eight-week digital psychoeducation program covering mental health, emotions, sleep, and healthy lifestyle habits.

Both groups will receive structured content through WhatsApp, three individual videoconference sessions with a psychologist, and access to asynchronous psychological support during the intervention.

The main objective is to determine whether Vínculo is more effective than digital psychoeducation in reducing insomnia severity, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms after eight weeks. Participants will also be assessed three and six months after the intervention to examine whether improvements are maintained. Additional assessments will examine daily functioning and psychological processes related to treatment outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Insomnia Symptom Severity (Insomnia Severity Index - ISI)
Depressive Symptom Severity (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 - PHQ-9)
Anxiety Symptom Severity (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 - GAD-7)
title: Vínculo: A Digital Intervention for Anxiety, Depression, and Insomnia Symptoms

brief_summary:
HEAL-TB (Health and Economic After-effects in Leicester Tuberculosis cohort) is a prospective observational study examining recovery among adults with pulmonary and extrapulmonary tuberculosis (TB). The study aims to understand how physical health, mental health, quality of life, daily activity, work and economic wellbeing change during TB treatment and up to 12 months after treatment completion.

Participants may join the study at different stages, from diagnosis until six months after completing TB treatment, and will be followed prospectively until 12 months after treatment completion. The study uses questionnaires, lung function testing, the Incremental Shuttle Walk Test, wrist-worn activity monitoring and information collected during routine clinical care. No experimental treatment is provided and participants continue to receive their usual NHS care.

The study aims to describe recovery over time, compare recovery following pulmonary and extrapulmonary TB, and identify factors associated with persistent health problems or poorer recovery.
primary_outcomes: Health-related quality of life measured by EQ-5D-5L
Physical activity measured by wrist-worn activity monitor
Work productivity and activity impairment measured by WPAI
title: Health and Economic After-effects in Leicester Tuberculosis Cohort

brief_summary:
This study aims to compare the effects of high-density and low-density single-session Pattern Scan Laser (PASCAL) panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR).

Panretinal photocoagulation is a standard treatment for proliferative diabetic retinopathy. However, the number of laser spots applied during a single treatment session varies in clinical practice. This study will investigate whether applying a higher number of laser spots in one session is as safe and effective as applying a lower number of spots, particularly regarding changes in central macular thickness.

Eligible patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy who have not previously received PRP will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. The low-density group will receive 2,200-3,000 laser spots, while the high-density group will receive 3,200-4,000 laser spots using the PASCAL laser system in a single session.

Central macular thickness will be measured using optical coherence tomography (OCT) before treatment and four weeks after treatment. The main purpose is to determine whether high-density PRP is not inferior to low-density PRP in terms of changes in central macular thickness. Visual acuity and treatment-related adverse effects will also be assessed.

The findings may help determine whether a higher number of laser spots can be safely delivered in a single PASCAL PRP session without causing an unacceptable increase in macular thickness.
title: High- Versus Low-Density PASCAL Laser Treatment for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy

brief_summary: This study is a prospective, randomized, single-blind, parallel-group, single-center clinical trial in adults undergoing elective laparoscopic surgery under general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation. It will compare sterile medical sodium hyaluronate gel with lidocaine cream as a lubricant applied to the distal portion and cuff surface of the endotracheal tube. The study aims to evaluate whether sodium hyaluronate gel is superior to lidocaine cream in reducing postoperative throat numbness. The primary outcome is throat numbness assessed using a visual analog scale (VAS) 30 minutes after surgery. Secondary outcomes include throat numbness at other specified time points, coughing during emergence and after the first oral water intake, postoperative sore throat, hoarseness, endotracheal tube cuff pressure, hemodynamic responses during intubation and extubation, satisfaction, and adverse events. A total of 120 participants are planned, with 60 participants in each group.
conditions: Postoperative Throat Numbness; Post-intubation Throat Symptoms
title: Sodium Hyaluronate Gel Versus Lidocaine Cream for Endotracheal Tube Lubrication

brief_summary:
Rotator cuff tears can cause shoulder pain, weakness, and difficulty with daily activities. Although arthroscopic rotator cuff repair helps many patients, recovery varies. Some patients continue to experience pain, shoulder stiffness, or incomplete tendon healing.

The REACT cohort will follow approximately 1,000 adults aged 18 to 75 years who are scheduled for their first arthroscopic rotator cuff repair at the Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, China. The study will examine how patients' health, lifestyle, shoulder imaging, tissue characteristics, surgical findings, and rehabilitation are associated with recovery.

Information will be collected before surgery and at 3, 6, 12, 24, and 60 months after surgery. Assessments will include shoulder symptoms and function, quality of life, physical examination, tendon healing on magnetic resonance imaging, additional treatments, and medical events. With appropriate consent, blood and small amounts of tissue that would otherwise be removed during routine surgery will be retained for laboratory research.

The investigators hypothesize that differences in clinical and biological characteristics identify rotator cuff tendinopathy subtypes associated with different recovery patterns. The study aims to improve classification and prediction of outcomes and to identify potential targets for future research. Treatment decisions will be made by patients and their treating clinicians as part of usual care. The study will not assign treatments, and computer-predicted candidate drugs will not be administered as part of this cohort.
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University, School of Medicine
title: Rotator Cuff Evaluation And Classification of Tendinopathy (REACT Cohort)

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to learn whether the Harmony Program, a community-based nursing intervention, can reduce loneliness in older adults living in the community. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the Harmony Program lower loneliness in older adults?
* Does the Harmony Program improve self-compassion and functional status (the ability to carry out daily activities independently)?

Researchers will compare older adults who take part in the Harmony Program with older adults who receive usual care to see if the program reduces loneliness.

Participants in the Harmony Program group will:

* Attend weekly 60-minute sessions for 12 weeks (8 group sessions followed by 4 individual sessions)
* Take part in health education, communication training, physical exercise, relaxation, self-compassion therapy, counseling, and a home visit with family involvement

Participants in both groups will complete questionnaires on loneliness, self-compassion, and daily functioning before the program and after 12 weeks.
primary_outcomes: Loneliness Measured by the UCLA Loneliness Scale Version 3
title: Harmony Nursing Intervention for Loneliness, Self-Compassion, and Functional Status Among Older Adults

brief_summary: This is a feasibility study. 20 non-ICU hospitalized patients at high risk of getting delirium will be consented and screened to receive a personalized multicomponent non-pharmacological intervention through an autonomous navigating robot at the bedside.
interventions: personalized multicomponent non-pharmacological intervention through an autonomous mobile robot to prevent delirium
primary_outcomes: Robot correctly arrived at the bedside and greeted the patient
Robot correctly arrived at the bedside, oriented the patient and delivered the personalized multicomponent non-pharmacological intervention.
