brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate whether combining an adductor canal block (ACB) with an infiltration between the popliteal artery and the knee capsule (IPACK) provides better postoperative analgesia than ACB alone in patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.

A total of 72 adult patients aged 18-50 years with American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status I-II will be randomly allocated into two groups. The intervention group will receive ultrasound-guided combined ACB and IPACK blocks, while the comparator group will receive ultrasound-guided ACB alone. Both groups will receive spinal anesthesia and standardized postoperative analgesia.

Postoperative pain intensity will be assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) at 2, 6, 12, and 24 hours after surgery. Other outcomes will include total opioid consumption during the first 24 hours, postoperative quality of recovery assessed by the QoR-15 questionnaire, time to first rescue analgesic request, maximum walking distance, and block-related complications.

The findings are expected to provide evidence on the effectiveness of adding an IPACK block to ACB to improve postoperative pain management following ACL reconstruction.
interventions: Ultrasound-Guided combined Adductor Canal Block plus IPACK Block
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain Intensity Measured by Numeric Rating Scale (NRS)
title: Comparison of Combined ACB and IPACK Versus ACB Alone for Postoperative Pain Management After ACL Reconstruction

brief_summary: This study is the first time BNT3211 will be tested in people. It will evaluate different dose levels of BNT3211 in adults to find suitable doses and to understand how safe the treatment is and how it may help people with advanced solid tumors.
primary_outcomes: Part A only - Occurrence of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) during the DLT evaluation period

Number of participants with treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs), Grade ≥3 TEAEs, serious adverse events (SAEs), treatment-related TEAEs, treatment-related Grade ≥3 TEAEs, and treatment-related SAEs
Number of participants with dose interruptions, reductions, or discontinuations of study treatment due to TEAEs
Part B only - Objective response rate
title: A First-in-human, Dose Escalation, and Expansion Study of BNT3211 for Participants With Advanced Solid Tumors

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of enhanced expiratory rebreathing space (EERS) therapy compared with conventional automatic positive airway pressure (APAP) therapy in patients with cardiovascular disease and complex sleep apnea (CompSA).

This is a prospective, single-center, randomized controlled trial involving 40 participants aged 18-75 years. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to either the EERS group or the conventional APAP group in a 1:1 ratio. Participants in the EERS group will receive individualized EERS therapy guided by overnight sleep monitoring, while those in the control group will receive conventional APAP therapy.

Each participant will be followed for five weeks, including a one-week screening period, a two-week treatment period, and a two-week follow-up period. The primary outcome is the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), which measures the number of breathing interruptions per hour of sleep, assessed after two weeks of treatment. Additional outcomes include other sleep-related breathing measures, cardiovascular health indicators, treatment adherence, comfort, and adverse events.

The findings may help determine whether EERS therapy is an effective and safe treatment option for complex sleep apnea in patients with cardiovascular disease.
lead_sponsor: Chinese Pulmonary Vascular Disease Research Group
primary_outcomes: Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) After Two Weeks of Treatment
title: Enhanced Expiratory Rebreathing Space Therapy for Complex Sleep Apnea in Patients With Cardiovascular Disease

brief_summary:
Caffeine (CAF) and New Zealand blackcurrant extract (NZBC) are nutritional supplements that have been investigated for their potential effects on endurance exercise performance, energy metabolism, and cognitive function. Caffeine is a stimulant that may improve endurance performance, alertness, and perceived exertion during exercise, while NZBC contains anthocyanins that may influence fat oxidation and physiological responses during endurance exercise. Although previous research has examined these supplements individually, limited research has investigated their combined effects. This study examined their independent and combined effects on endurance exercise performance, substrate oxidation, and cognitive function in healthy, endurance-trained women aged 18-40 years. Endurance exercise performance was the primary outcome, while substrate oxidation and cognitive function were secondary outcomes.

The study used a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover design involving four experimental conditions: placebo (PL; 600 mg maltodextrin), NZBC (600 mg containing 210 mg anthocyanins), CAF (6 mg/kg body weight), and NZBC+CAF at the same respective doses. Participants completed the conditions in a randomized order, with seven-day supplementation periods separated by seven-day washout intervals to minimize potential carryover effects. Neither participants nor researchers conducting the assessments knew which treatment was administered.

During each experimental testing session, participants first underwent body weight, resting heart rate, and blood pressure measurements before ingesting their final assigned supplement dose under researcher supervision. After a two-hour waiting period, participants completed a cognitive function assessment and questionnaires evaluating readiness to perform using a visual analog scale (VAS), caffeine consumption, and sleep quality. Blood lactate, glucose, and ratings of perceived exertion (RPE) were measured before a treadmill running test assessing endurance exercise performance and time to exhaustion. During exercise, RPE was recorded every three minutes, while respiratory gas exchange measurements were used to determine carbohydrate oxidation, fat oxidation, maximal fat oxidation, and energy expenditure. Blood lactate and glucose concentrations were measured immediately and five minutes after exercise, and heart rate and blood pressure were assessed one minute after exercise.
interventions: Caffeine and New Zealand Blackcurrant Extract
primary_outcomes: Time to Exhaustion During Treadmill Running (Minutes)
Maximal Fat Oxidation During Treadmill Running (g/min)
Carbon Dioxide Production During Treadmill Running (L/min)
title: Effects of Caffeine and New Zealand Blackcurrant on Endurance Performance in Women

brief_summary:
This retrospective study examined whether adding serum magnesium to the routine admission laboratory panel changes physicians' subsequent laboratory testing and prescribing practices.

Electronic hospital records from the Department of Internal Medicine and Geriatrics at Evangelisches Klinikum Bethel, Bielefeld, Germany, were evaluated. Patients admitted before and after the change in the admission laboratory panel were compared. The principal outcome was the proportion of patients undergoing deliberate serum magnesium measurement during hospitalization (either de novo testing or repeat testing). Additional outcomes included the number of repeat magnesium testing and the initiation of magnesium or related electrolyte prescriptions.

Weekly data were analyzed using interrupted time-series methods.
interventions: Addition of serum magnesium testing to the routine admission laboratory panel
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients with at least one separately ordered serum magnesium measurement.
title: Magnesium Testing and Prescribing Before and After Adding Magnesium to Routine Admission Laboratory Tests

brief_summary:
The goal of this open pilot study is to learn whether FTTN is effective in treating mental health problems in adult children of World War 2-survivors, who attribute their symptoms of anxiety, mood and/or personality problems to their parents' war trauma.

Participants will:

* Participate in the FTNN intervention.
* Answer questionnaires three times over five months: before starting FTTN, directly after completing FTTN, and two months after finishing FTTN.
* Participate in an interview twice: before starting FTNN and directly after completing FTNN.
title: From There Towards Now; Intervention for Jewish and Indonesian Post-war Generations

brief_summary:
This single-center, single-arm phase I/II pilot study evaluates the safety and feasibility of single-fraction stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) with a simultaneous integrated boost to the dominant intraprostatic lesion (DIL) in men with localized prostate cancer.

Ten participants with very low-, low-, or favorable intermediate-risk prostate adenocarcinoma and an MRI-visible DIL (PI-RADS 4-5) will be enrolled. After hydrogel rectal spacer insertion, patients receive MR-guided SBRT on an MR-Linac in one fraction: 20 Gy to the whole prostate, 26 Gy to the DIL, and 15 Gy to the seminal vesicles. The aim is to deliver a brachytherapy-like ablative dose without an invasive procedure.

The primary outcome is acute genitourinary and rectal toxicity (CTCAE v5.0) within 3 months after treatment. Secondary outcomes include late toxicity, patient-reported quality of life (IPSS, IIEF, FACT-P), biochemical failure-free survival (Phoenix definition), local recurrence-free, progression-free, distant metastasis-free and overall survival, correlation of MR-radiomics with clinical outcomes, and cost-effectiveness. Patients will be followed for 5 years.
interventions: Single-fraction MR-guided SBRT 20 Gy with simultaneous integrated boost to the dominant intraprostatic lesion 26 Gy
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Acute toxicity (Genitourinary and Gastrointestinal toxicity)
title: DOTA-1: Single-Fraction MR-guided Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy for Localized Prostate Cancer

brief_summary: This study investigates the effects of a dual glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptor agonist, tirzepatide, on corneal nerve morphology and other ocular parameters in adults with obesity. Participants, adult patients with obesity, will receive either tirzepatide or placebo over 24 weeks. Researchers will assess ophthalmological clinical status, corneal nerve changes, ocular surface, intraocular pressure, anterior-segment biometry and optical coherent tomography, and exophthalmometry. Orbital MRI will be performed in a subgroup of participants receiving tirzepatide. Optical coherence tomography and Optical coherence tomography angiography will be preformed to asses the posterior segment. The goal of this study is to investigate the effects of tirzepatide on corneal nerve morphology and functional consequences, as well as anterior segment parameters, during tirzepatide-induced weight loss, addressing an important gap in understanding the impact of incretin-based therapies on corneal nerves and anatomy of anterior eye segment.
title: Effects of Tirzepatide on Corneal Nerve Morphology and Other Ocular Parameters in Adults With Obesity

brief_summary: The study is being conducted to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and ORR of HRS-7172 combined with other antitumor therapies in subjects with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer; Evaluate the pharmacokinetic (PK) characteristics of HRS-7172 and other efficacy endpoints for the treatment of locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer.
primary_outcomes: The incidence and severity of adverse events (AE)/serious adverse events (SAE) (rated based on CTCAE v6.0)
title: A Phase II Clinical Study of HRS-7172 as Monotherapy or in Combination With Anti-Tumor Therapy in Participants With Advanced Lung Cancer to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability, and Efficacy

brief_summary:
Anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury (AT-DILI) is a common side effect of tuberculosis (TB) treatment. It often forces TB drugs to be stopped temporarily, which may reduce treatment success. N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is an antioxidant that helps the body make glutathione and may help the liver recover. Most previous studies tested NAC to prevent liver injury rather than to treat liver injury that has already occurred.

This study aimed to find out whether oral NAC, given as an adjuvant therapy, improves liver function and nausea-vomiting in hospitalized adults with drug-susceptible TB who developed AT-DILI. Participants were randomly assigned to receive effervescent NAC 600 mg twice daily for 7 days or no NAC. Liver tests (ALT, AST, and total bilirubin) were measured on days 0, 3, 6, and 9, and nausea and vomiting were assessed daily from day 0 to day 9.
title: N-Acetylcysteine as Adjuvant Therapy for Drug-Induced Hepatitis in Hospitalized Tuberculosis Patients

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled study will compare the effectiveness of oral itraconazole alone with a combination of oral itraconazole and terbinafine in adults with resistant tinea corporis (ringworm of the body). Resistant tinea corporis is a fungal skin infection that persists despite appropriate topical antifungal treatment or returns shortly after treatment.

Eligible patients aged 18-60 years with resistant tinea corporis confirmed by potassium hydroxide (KOH) microscopy will be randomly assigned to receive either oral itraconazole alone or oral itraconazole combined with terbinafine. Treatment response will be assessed clinically and by KOH microscopy.

The main purpose of the study is to determine whether the combination of itraconazole and terbinafine is more effective than itraconazole alone in achieving complete clinical and mycological cure after eight weeks of treatment. Patients who achieve treatment success will also be followed for a further four weeks to assess whether the infection returns.

The study hypothesis is that there is a difference in treatment efficacy between combined itraconazole with terbinafine and itraconazole alone in patients with resistant tinea corporis.
title: Comparing Itraconazole Alone With Itraconazole Plus Terbinafine for Adults With Resistant Tinea Corporis

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn about the clinical characteristics, natural course, and long-term outcomes of valvular heart disease in children and adults of all ages. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How many participants die from any cause or are hospitalized for heart failure within 5 years?
* How does valvular heart disease change over time, and how do different causes, severity levels, other medical conditions, and treatments affect long-term outcomes?

Participants with valvular heart disease will:

* Receive their regular medical care, which may include medications, surgery, or catheter-based procedures (the study does not change any treatment)
* Have their medical records, laboratory tests, and heart imaging results collected
* Attend follow-up visits at 6 months, 12 months, and then once a year
* Be asked to provide extra blood samples during routine blood draws, and leftover valve or heart tissue from clinically indicated procedures, only if they agree (this is optional)
lead_sponsor: First Affiliated Hospital Xi'an Jiaotong University
primary_outcomes: Time to First All-Cause Death or Unplanned Hospitalization for Heart Failure
title: Clinical Characteristics and Long-Term Outcomes of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease

brief_summary:
The goal of this project is to implement the co-created technical assistance program (developed through the CA CBO Theory of Change) in a clustered randomized waitlist controlled trial conducted with leaders/managers and staff in participating CBOs.

Additionally, using mixed methods approaches, the project seeks to assess the impact of the technical assistance program on multilevel outcomes for a) clients, b) CHW and other outreach staff, and c) CBO leadership
conditions: Study is Focused on Social Need and Not a Single Disease or Condition
title: California Community Engagement Alliance: A California Consortium to Enhance Social Needs Care for Individuals Facing Economic or Access-Related Constraints, Including Populations With Limited Service Access

brief_summary:
Almost all patients who receive radiotherapy for head and neck cancer develop a skin reaction in the treated area, known as acute radiation-induced skin injury (aRISI), also called acute radiation dermatitis. Mild reactions cause redness, itching and peeling; severe reactions can be painful, may interrupt cancer treatment, and reduce quality of life. The most commonly used preventive creams are topical glucocorticosteroids (steroids). These can help, but prolonged use of topical steroids carries its own risks, such as skin thinning and small visible blood vessels, which is a particular concern on the delicate skin of the head and neck during a six- to seven-week course of radiotherapy.

Topical calcineurin inhibitors, such as tacrolimus, are steroid-free anti-inflammatory creams that have been used safely for more than 20 years in other inflammatory skin conditions (for example, atopic dermatitis), including long-term "proactive" application to prevent flares. Because radiation skin injury and these conditions share similar inflammatory mechanisms, tacrolimus is a biologically plausible, steroid-sparing alternative for preventing or treating aRISI. To date, however, it has not been tested for this purpose in a randomized trial.

This single-center, randomized trial in adults undergoing radiotherapy (alone or combined with chemotherapy or other systemic treatment) for head and neck cancer evaluates whether topical tacrolimus can prevent or delay aRISI and whether it is as effective as, and better tolerated than, topical steroids. Participants are randomly assigned to one of four groups that differ in the cream applied preventively ("proactively") from the first day of radiotherapy and the cream applied to treat an established reaction ("reactively"):

Group 1 (standard of care): no preventive cream; mometasone (a potent steroid) if a reaction develops.

Group 2: preventive hydrocortisone (a mild steroid); mometasone reactively. Group 3: no preventive cream; tacrolimus reactively. Group 4: preventive tacrolimus; tacrolimus reactively.

All participants also follow a standardized skin-care routine (emollient and sun protection). The preventive cream is applied twice weekly from the first day of radiotherapy until two weeks after it ends; the reactive cream is applied once daily once a reaction appears. Skin reactions are graded regularly using standard scales (RTOG and CTCAE). For safety, the study cream is stopped if a severe (grade 3) reaction develops, and the patient is kept under close monitoring and managed according to current recommendations.

The main outcome is the time from the start of radiotherapy to the first visible skin reaction (grade 1 or higher). Other outcomes include the time to more severe reactions, the maximum severity reached, how quickly reactions progress once they start, treatment side effects, and patient-reported quality of life. By directly comparing a steroid-free calcineurin inhibitor with topical steroids and standard care, the study aims to provide the first randomized evidence on whether tacrolimus can safely delay or reduce radiation-induced skin injury in head and neck cancer, and to guide the design of larger confirmatory trials.
primary_outcomes: Time from start of radiotherapy to first acute radiation-induced skin injury (aRISI), RTOG grade >=1
title: Proactive Therapy of Acute Radiation-induced Skin Injury in Head and Neck Cancer

brief_summary:
1. Research background: Measurement, analysis, and in vitro simulation of patient-specific mandibular functional movement constitute one of the key steps in prosthodontic treatment, among which the recording and simulation of protrusive movement are essential components. The path of the condyle during mandibular protrusion is governed by the anatomical features of the temporomandibular joint. When the mandible moves forward, the condyle travels anteroinferiorly within the glenoid fossa; this trajectory is defined as the protrusive condylar path. The angle formed between the protrusive condylar path and the Frankfort horizontal plane is the protrusive condylar path inclination, a critical parameter for characterizing mandibular protrusive movement. Transferring this biological condylar path inclination to an articulator yields the sagittal condylar inclination (SCI), which is represented on the articulator as the angle between the condylar guide groove in the sagittal plane and the reference plane of the articulator. Accurate SCI measurement is of great importance for clinical treatment planning and the fabrication of functional prostheses. Conventional SCI measurement involves multiple procedures: physical facebow transfer, acquisition of stone casts and protrusive interocclusal records, and SCI reading on a mechanical articulator. This workflow is highly technique-sensitive, and its accuracy is susceptible to operator experience, as well as the precision of cast and recording materials. Furthermore, mechanical facebow transfer and conventional impression-taking tend to cause patient discomfort. With advances in digital technology, electronic facebows, which offer high accuracy and favorable repeatability, have been adopted for patient-specific SCI acquisition. Nevertheless, their high cost and relatively cumbersome clinical workflow hinder widespread clinical adoption. Emerging techniques employ a facial scanner to track real-time spatial displacements of intraoral fiducial points. Facial scan data and dental model scans are registered and fused via facial landmarks to visualize and capture the true kinematic trajectories of the mandible and bilateral condyles, with SCI values generated directly. This approach eliminates the need for a facebow or head-mounted apparatus and may confer superior patient comfort. However, studies validating the accuracy of SCI measurements obtained with this workflow remain scarce. Therefore, this study took electronic facebow tracing data as the control to evaluate the accuracy of a fully digital SCI measurement protocol based on Shining intraoral and facial scanning in edentulous patients, providing evidence for the selection of clinical SCI measurement strategies and further optimization of fully digital SCI acquisition technology.
2. Research objective: To investigate the differences in sagittal condylar inclination (SCI) measured using virtual facebow and virtual interocclusal records versus electronic facebow tracing data during definitive implant rehabilitation of edentulous patients, so as to provide evidence for clinical practice.
3. Study design and methods: Design type: prospective, interventional, single-center, randomized controlled non-inferiority study.Study duration: 2 years. Start time: From the date of adoption of ethics. End time: 2028. Edentulous patients who met the eligibility criteria were screened from those receiving implant-supported full-arch provisional restorations and scheduled for definitive rehabilitation at the Stomatological Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, from the date of ethical approval to August 2028. At the time of definitive impression taking, mandibular movement trajectories were captured and left and right sagittal condylar inclination (SCI) values were recorded using the Zebris electronic facebow and the Shining intraoral and facial scanning system, respectively. All measurements were performed by a single experienced operator. Each measurement method was repeated three times per participant, and the average value was calculated for analysis.
title: Comparison Evaluation of the Accuracy of Two Digital Technologies of Measuring Sagittal Condylar Inclination in Edentulous Patients

brief_summary: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with macrovascular tumor thrombus carries a poor prognosis, and systemic therapy alone provides limited benefit in this population. This single-center, single-arm, phase 2 trial evaluates the efficacy and safety of a regimen combining chemotherapy-minimized, blank microsphere-based transarterial chemoembolization (BMS-TACE), low-dose lenvatinib, the anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific antibody iparomlimab and tuvonralimab, and stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT). In BMS-TACE, blank microspheres are the principal embolic agent and chemotherapy is used only as an adjunct at a fixed, minimal dose (doxorubicin 10 mg and lobaplatin 10 mg), in order to limit chemotherapy-related liver injury and systemic toxicity and to allow repeated embolization in patients with limited hepatic reserve. Forty-two participants with BCLC stage C HCC and tumor thrombus in the main portal vein or superior mesenteric vein (Vp3/Vp4), hepatic vein, or inferior vena cava, without extrahepatic metastases, will be enrolled. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review using mRECIST.
primary_outcomes: Progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review (BICR) using mRECIST
title: Chemotherapy-Minimized Blank Microsphere Transarterial Embolization (BMS-TACE) Plus Low-Dose Lenvatinib, Iparomlimab and Tuvonralimab, and SBRT in Hepatocellular Carcinoma With Macrovascular Tumor Thrombus

brief_summary: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of Glumetinib plus Osimertinib in patients with non-small cell lung cancer with classic EGFR mutations and MET overexpression or amplification.
title: A Study of Glumetinib in Combination With Osimertinib as 1st Line Treatment in Patients With Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary: Persistent Postural Perceptual Dizziness (PPPD) is the leading cause of chronic dizziness, with symptoms frequently triggered during situations causing visual overload (e.g. supermarket aisles, crowded spaces, and riding an escalator). The current treatments include cognitive physical therapy and antidepressant medication to relieve anxiety and depression symptoms, but these do not directly target symptoms of visual overload. Whilst the benefits of mindfulness on other neurological disorders characterised by visual disturbances (e.g. visual snow syndrome) have been reported, the effects of mindfulness on visual symptoms associated with PPPD have not been explored. This paper will present the protocol of a two-arm parallel group randomised feasibility study, examining feasibility of recruitment, acceptability and potential benefits of a mindfulness-based visualisation intervention in PPPD. The primary objective of this study is to explore the feasibility of mindfulness-based visualisation as a treatment in visual subtypes across a cohort of PPPD patients.
title: Online Mindfulness-based Visualisation to Treat Visual Overload in Persistent Postural Perceptual Dizziness (PPPD).

brief_summary:
Researchers are looking for new ways to treat macular edema after retinal vein occlusion (ME-RVO). ME-RVO happens when a vein becomes blocked in the retina, the back part of the eye. This blockage causes fluid to leak into the macula, which is the part of the retina that helps to see fine details. The buildup of fluid, called macular edema, can cause blurry vision.

In this trial, researchers want to learn if a trial medicine called MK-8748 can treat ME-RVO. A standard (usual) treatment for ME-RVO is aflibercept. However, standard treatments such as aflibercept may not work for every person.

The main goal of this trial is to learn if participants who receive MK-8748 can see as clearly as participants who receive aflibercept.
primary_outcomes: Mean Change in Best-Corrected Visual Acuity (BCVA) (Early Treatment of Diabetic Retinopathy Study [ETDRS] Letters) From Baseline to Week 24
title: A Clinical Trial of MK-8748 Compared to Aflibercept in Participants With Macular Edema After Retinal Vein Occlusion (MK-8748-006)

brief_summary:
To compare the analgesic efficacy, patient quality of life and safety profile of celiac plexus neurolysis versus splanchnic neurolysis in patients of abdominal malignancies.

Sixty patients suffering from abdominal malignancies. Patients in Group C were administered celiac plexus neurolysis while those in Group S were administered bilateral splanchnic neurolysis. The primary outcome was the pain score measured by the Visual analogue score at two, four and eight and twelve weeks following the procedure. The secondary outcome was improvement in patient quality of life using SF12 questionnaire and safety profile of the procedure.
primary_outcomes: Change in pain intensity on the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) from baseline
title: Celiac Versus Splanchnic Neurolysis in Abdominal Malignancies

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to observe the efficacy and safety of inebilizumab in the treatment of IgG4-related disease. The main question it aims to answer the optimal steroid-sparing regimen for patients with IgG4-RD in clinical practice.

This study will enroll all patients with IgG4-RD treated with inebilizumab. Enrolled patients will receive different treatment regimens according to disease severity and whether they are taking other immunosuppressive agents.
title: Real-world Evidence of Inebilizumab in IgG4-RD

brief_summary: This randomized, open-label trial compared an ultrasound-guided serratus anterior plane (SAP) block performed at the third rib level at the end of surgery plus fentanyl patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) with PCA alone in women undergoing breast cancer surgery with an axillary procedure. The primary outcome was cumulative PCA fentanyl consumption in the first 12 postoperative hours.
title: Serratus Anterior Plane Block at the Third Rib Level After Breast Cancer Surgery With Axillary Intervention

brief_summary: KH658 is a adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector-based gene therapy for suprachoroidal space injection. The long-term, stable therapeutic protein after one time injection for DR could potentially reduce the treatment burden and maintain visual acuity and retinal anatomical stability
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants with a ≥2 steps DRSS Improvement From Baseline in Diabetic Retinopthy
Proportion of Participants Developing Vision-Threatening Events (VTEs)
title: Safty and Efficacy of KH658 in Subjects With Diabetic Retinopathy

brief_summary:
Postpartum constipation is a common problem that can affect women's comfort and quality of life after childbirth. This study aims to evaluate whether Pilates exercises can help improve constipation symptoms in women after vaginal delivery.

A total of 40 women aged 22-35 years with postpartum constipation will participate in this study. Participants will be randomly assigned to two groups, with 20 women in each group. The first group will receive a supervised Pilates exercise program in addition to standard postpartum care, while the second group will receive standard postpartum care alone.

The Pilates program will last for 9 weeks, with three supervised sessions per week. Standard postpartum care will include advice about healthy eating, adequate fluid intake, dietary fiber, and physical activity.

Constipation symptoms, bowel habits, stool consistency, and constipation-related quality of life will be assessed before and after the intervention. The results of both groups will be compared to evaluate whether adding Pilates exercises to standard postpartum care improves postpartum constipation.
primary_outcomes: Change in Patient Assessment of Constipation Symptoms (PAC-SYM) Total Score
Change in Patient Assessment of Constipation Quality of Life (PAC-QOL) Total Score
title: Pilates Exercises for Postpartum Constipation

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn about the effects of electroacupuncture on exosome load and clinical outcomes in patients with fibromyalgia, a chronic condition characterized by widespread pain, fatigue, sleep disturbances, and cognitive dysfunction.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does acupuncture alter the load of circulating exosomes in patients with fibromyalgia?
2. Is a change in exosome load associated with improvements in pain, cognitive function, and sleep quality?
3. Can exosome load serve as a potential biomarker of brain-related changes in conditions involving chronic pain?

Participants with fibromyalgia receiving electroacupuncture as part of their routine clinical care will provide blood samples before and after treatment for exosome analysis. Participants will also undergo assessments of mechanical pain threshold, pain intensity, overall symptom burden, cognitive function (using objective neuropsychological tests and self-report questionnaires), and sleep quality. Healthy volunteers will be included as a comparison group.
primary_outcomes: Brain-derived exosomes - Changes in exosomal load
title: The Effect of Acupuncture on Brain-Derived Exosomal Load, Cognitive Function, and Sleep Disturbances in Patients With Fibromyalgia.

brief_summary: The Philippines is considering a mandatory front-of-package label (FoPL) for packaged foods. This randomized controlled trial will test which label design best helps consumers avoid products high in sugar, sodium, or saturated fat. Adults who buy packaged foods will be approached outside supermarkets and other food retailers in three locations: the City of Manila, Iloilo City, and the Municipality of San Jose, Dinagat Islands. After consent, each participant will be randomly assigned to one of five groups and will view mock packaged food products on a tablet: no label (control), a Nutrient Warning Label, a Multiple Traffic Light label, a Health Star Rating, or a Nutri-Grade style label. The main outcome is how likely participants say the participant is to buy products that contain nutrients of concern in excess. The study will also measure whether participants can correctly identify which nutrients are in excess, which of two similar products the participant would buy, and which product the participant thinks is healthier. Results will inform FoPL policy in the Philippines.
lead_sponsor: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health
primary_outcomes: Mean Self-Reported Intent to Purchase Products Containing Nutrients of Concern in Excess
title: Effect of Front-of-Package Labels on Intent to Purchase Packaged Foods in the Philippines

brief_summary: This is a multicenter phase 1/2 clinical study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of SYS6043 monotherapy or SYS6043 combined with PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody ± chemotherapy in patients with advanced solid tumors.
interventions: SYS6043 combined with PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody ± chemotherapy.
title: A Phase I/II Clinical Trial of SYS6043 Monotherapy or SYS6043 Combined With PD-1/VEGF Bispecific Antibody ± Chemotherapy in the Treatment of Advanced Solid Tumors.

brief_summary:
The goal of this parallel-group cluster randomized clinical trial is to evaluate whether opportunistic screening for left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD), using an artificial intelligence algorithm applied to electrocardiograms (AI-ECG), increases the detection of previously unrecognized LVSD among adults aged ≥40 years receiving routine care in primary healthcare centers within the Brazilian Public Health System. LVSD is a key finding in the diagnosis of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), a condition for which effective guideline-directed medical therapies are available but which remains underdiagnosed and undertreated.

The study will also evaluate the effects of AI-ECG screening on clinical management, healthcare utilization, implementation outcomes, and healthcare costs.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

1. Does adding AI-ECG screening to usual clinical assessment increase the proportion of patients with newly identified LVSD (left ventricular ejection fraction \<50%) within six months compared with clinical assessment alone?
2. Does AI-ECG screening improve the use of echocardiography, the recognition by primary care teams, and the initiation or optimization of guideline-directed medical therapy for HFrEF?
3. How do LVSD detection rates differ between patients identified through AI-ECG screening alone and those identified through clinical suspicion alone?
4. Is this screening strategy feasible, acceptable, and cost-effective when implemented in primary healthcare?

Primary healthcare centers will be randomized to either an intervention group, in which AI-ECG screening results will be provided alongside the standard ECG report, or a control group receiving usual care without AI-ECG results.

Participants will:

1. Undergo a routine 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG), as clinically indicated by their primary care physician.
2. Be referred for echocardiography based on clinical suspicion of LVSD in both groups or, additionally, a positive AI-ECG screening result in the intervention group.
3. Receive educational materials about HFrEF if newly diagnosed, while participating healthcare professionals will receive educational interventions on heart failure diagnosis and management.
4. Complete questionnaires evaluating educational interventions, when applicable.
5. Be followed for six months to assess newly identified LVSD, treatment initiation and optimization, healthcare utilization (including emergency visits and hospitalizations), mortality, implementation outcomes, and healthcare costs.
interventions: Artificial Intelligence applied to the electrocardiogram to identify left ventricular systolic dysfunction
primary_outcomes: Proportion of new diagnosis of left ventricular systolic dysfunction
title: AI-ECG Screening for Early Heart Failure Diagnosis

brief_summary: This proposal will test whether repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) modulation of the brain's posterior default mode network (pDMN) will alter alcohol craving, alcohol seeking and impulsivity in men and women who have an alcohol use disorder but are not seeking treatment.
primary_outcomes: Change in pDMN BOLD responses to alcohol taste after iTBS, cTBS or sham treatment.
Change in cue-induced craving after TBS.
Change in the number of completed trials and alcohol infusions earned on a progressive ratio task after TBS.
Change in impulsivity assessed using a delay discounting task after TBS.
Change in pDMN BOLD responses during a delay discounting task after TBS.
title: Posterior Default Network Modulation in Alcohol Use Disorder

brief_summary: This study aims to retrospectively evaluate the clinical effectiveness and safety of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in treating patients with functional constipation (FC) who also have type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). It analyzes changes in bowel function, glucose metabolism indicators, and gut microbiota structure before and after FMT, and further explores the relationship between donor-related microbiota remodeling, predicted microbial metabolic functions, and clinical outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Change in spontaneous bowel movement (SBM) frequency
title: Exploring the Use of Fecal Microbiota Transplantation in Treating Diabetes-Related Constipation

brief_summary:
The purpose of this Phase 2 study is:

1. to evaluate the efficacy, safety and tolerability of DDY391 in participants with moderate to severe active rheumatoid arthritis (RA).
2. to provide information about dose selection and study design for subsequent clinical development.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants achieving American College of Rheumatology 50 (ACR50) response
title: A Study to Assess the Efficacy, Safety and Tolerability of DDY391 in Participants With Rheumatoid Arthritis

brief_summary: Breast cancer surgery can cause pain and altered sensation in the armpit and upper arm. During modified radical mastectomy, a nerve called the intercostobrachial nerve may be preserved or cut while lymph nodes are removed from the armpit. This randomized study will compare postoperative pain and the time required for axillary dissection between these two approaches. Thirty-four female patients aged 18 to 75 years with stage I or II breast cancer who are undergoing modified radical mastectomy will be assigned to two groups of 17 participants each. Pain will be assessed after surgery and during follow-up for three months, and the duration of axillary dissection will be measured during the operation. The study aims to assess whether preservation of the nerve is associated with less postoperative pain without a substantial increase in dissection time.
interventions: Intercostobrachial Nerve Preservation During Modified Radical Mastectomy
Intercostobrachial Nerve Transection During Modified Radical Mastectomy
title: Intercostobrachial Nerve Preservation Versus Transection During Modified Radical Mastectomy

brief_summary: This clinical study aims to establish standardised image acquisition and analysis methods using Antera 3D for the quantitative assessment of atrophic scars.
primary_outcomes: Test-retest repeatability of Depression Volume Measured Using Antera 3D
title: Methodological Validation of Antera 3D for Quantitative Assessment of Atrophic Scars

brief_summary:
This study observes patients with ankylosing spondylitis (AS) who are receiving, or have received, multiple infusions of allogeneic invariant natural killer T (iNKT) cells as a treatment. Allogeneic iNKT cells are immune cells taken from a healthy donor, grown in the laboratory, and given to patients by infusion.

The treatment infusions are given under a separate treatment protocol. This study does not give any treatment. It only collects blood samples and analyzes them to learn how the immune system changes during and after the cell infusions.

Researchers will study two main questions: (1) how iNKT cell subsets and the overall immune cell network in the blood change over time, and (2) what the iNKT cells look like at the single-cell level, including their transcriptional (gene expression) profiles and clonal evolution..

Participants will provide blood samples at scheduled study visits for up to 52 weeks. The goal is to better understand how allogeneic iNKT cell therapy reshapes the immune system in AS, which may help guide future treatment studies.
primary_outcomes: Change in Peripheral Blood iNKT Cell Subset Polarization During Multiple Infusions of Allogeneic iNKT Cells
Change in Peripheral Blood Immune Network Remodeling During Multiple Infusions of Allogeneic iNKT Cells
title: Allogeneic iNKT Cells in AS: Immune Remodeling Study

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of single ascending dose of QLS7402 injection administered subcutaneously in adult participants with overweight or obesity
lead_sponsor: Shanghai Qilu Pharmaceutical Research and Development Center LTD
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs)
Number of participants with treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs)
Number of participants with serious adverse events (SAEs)
Number of participants with abnormal physical examination, 12-lead ECG and clinical laboratory tests
title: A Phase 1 Study of QLS7402 Injection in Adult Participants With Overweight or Obesity

brief_summary:
This study will examine what happens to children aged 3 months to 5 years after hospital discharge following severe malaria or severe malarial anaemia (a very low blood level caused by malaria). It will take place at Newala District Hospital in Tanzania.

Researchers will review hospital records from the previous two years. They will also follow 250 children for 12 weeks after hospital discharge.

The study will examine:

1. Whether children die or return to hospital after discharge.
2. Whether children experience malaria again after discharge.
3. How children's blood levels recover after severe illness.
4. The healthcare services families use and the costs they face.

Researchers will also interview caregivers, community health workers and healthcare providers. These interviews will explore experiences, challenges and support available to children after hospital discharge.

The findings will help improve understanding of children's recovery after severe malaria. They may also inform future approaches to follow-up care and support for affected children.

This is an observational study. Researchers will not give participants any study medicine or additional treatment.
primary_outcomes: Anaemia recovery among children with SMA at baseline.
title: Understanding the Burden and Post-Discharge Management of Severe Malarial Anaemia and Severe Malaria Among Tanzanian Children: An Epidemiological and Qualitative Study

brief_summary:
Postoperative gut microbiota dysbiosis is a common clinical concern in patients undergoing rectal cancer surgery and may contribute to gastrointestinal dysfunction and postoperative complications. Inulin-based compound prebiotics may help maintain intestinal microbial balance by promoting beneficial bacteria and modulating gut microbial composition. However, their efficacy and safety in preventing postoperative gut microbiota dysbiosis in patients with rectal cancer remain to be established.

This study is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm clinical trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of inulin-based compound prebiotics in preventing gut microbiota dysbiosis following radical rectal cancer surgery and to assess their effects on gut microbiota composition.

A total of 261 adult patients with histologically confirmed rectal adenocarcinoma undergoing laparoscopic radical rectal cancer surgery with a protective intestinal stoma will be enrolled at three study centers. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to one of three groups: (1) inulin-based compound prebiotics combined with probiotics, (2) probiotics combined with placebo, or (3) placebo alone. Study interventions will be administered from postoperative day 1 through day 5.

The primary outcome is the incidence of gut microbiota dysbiosis within five days after surgery. Secondary outcomes include changes in gut microbiota composition and diversity, inflammatory markers, and fecal short-chain fatty acid levels. Gut microbiota will be assessed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing and metagenomic sequencing. Safety will be evaluated through the monitoring and recording of adverse events throughout the intervention period.

This study aims to provide clinical evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of inulin-based compound prebiotics for preventing postoperative gut microbiota dysbiosis and their potential role in modulating intestinal microbial homeostasis in patients undergoing rectal cancer surgery.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Postoperative Gut Microbiota Dysbiosis
title: Effects of Inulin-Based Prebiotics on Gut Microbiota After Rectal Cancer Surgery

brief_summary:
During some operations on the abdominal aorta, the surgeon needs to temporarily clamp the aorta above the arteries that supply the kidneys. This can reduce blood flow to the kidneys and may cause acute kidney injury.

This study will follow 50 adults at Policlinico di Sant'Orsola in Bologna, Italy. During their operation, a temporary shunt will perfuse blood from humeral artery to the renal arteries. The treating surgeon decides whether to use the shunt as part of clinical care, independently of study participation.

The researchers will record how often kidney injury occurs in the first 7 days after surgery and how often problems related to the shunt, kidney arteries or arm access occur within 30 days. They will also track the need for dialysis, kidney function and survival over 12 months.
title: Kidney Blood Flow During Open Aortic Surgery (RENAL-SHUNT)

brief_summary:
This study investigates the safety and potential antitumor activity of LP-184 in patients with advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma.

LP-184 is an investigational anticancer drug designed to damage the DNA of cancer cells. Certain cancer cells may be particularly sensitive to LP-184 if they have impaired DNA repair mechanisms and express a protein called PTGR1, which is involved in activating the drug.

The study aims to investigate whether LP-184 can be safely administered and whether it can reduce tumor growth in patients whose tumors have these specific characteristics.

The study consists of two parts. Phase Ib will evaluate the safety and tolerability of LP-184 and determine the recommended dose for Phase II. Phase II will investigate the antitumor activity of LP-184 by assessing tumor response to treatment.

All participants will receive LP-184 intravenously on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day treatment cycle. Up to 39 patients will be enrolled in the study.

brief_summary:
This study aims to explore a new, non-invasive treatment to help patients recover upper limb motor function after a stroke. Many stroke survivors experience long-term movement difficulties, and standard physical therapies may not always be effective, especially for those with severe motor impairments. Previous research suggests that stimulating a specific deep brain region called the cerebellar dentate nucleus can promote motor recovery, but traditional methods require invasive surgery.

In this study, researchers will investigate a novel technology called Temporal Interference (TI) electrical stimulation. TI allows researchers to safely and painlessly stimulate deep brain areas from the scalp without any surgery or implanted electrodes. The research team will enroll 10 patients who experienced a stroke 1 to 3 years ago and still have moderate to severe upper limb weakness. Participants will receive TI stimulation therapy 5 times a week for 4 weeks. Before, during, and after the treatment period, the researchers will use clinical physical assessments, brain imaging (fMRI), and non-invasive brain monitoring (EEG and fNIRS) to evaluate whether this treatment is safe, feasible, and effective for improving upper limb movement in chronic stroke survivors.
primary_outcomes: The safety of the tTIS intervention
title: DN-tTIS for Post-Stroke Motor Recovery

This prospective observational cohort study will examine the association between obesity and myopia in children and adolescents. Approximately 600 participants aged 6 to 18 years will be enrolled at the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University, including 300 participants with obesity and 300 participants with a body mass index within the normal range.

Participants will not be assigned to any study intervention. The study will collect information from body measurements, body composition assessments, eye examinations, lifestyle questionnaires, follow-up assessments, and existing clinical records. The investigators will evaluate whether obesity-related measures, including body mass index, body mass index z-score, body fat percentage, and visceral fat, are associated with myopia, axial length, refractive status, and changes in these outcomes over time. Lifestyle factors such as outdoor activity, near work, screen use, sleep, and diet will also be considered.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Axial Length
Change From Baseline in Spherical Equivalent Refractive Error
title: Association Between Childhood Obesity and Myopia: A Prospective Cohort Study

brief_summary: Knee osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint condition that leads to pain, functional limitations, and reduced quality of life, particularly in middle-aged adults. Core, hip and knee muscular weakness leads to altered biomechanics of the lower limb that enhance joint loading and worsens functional outcome. This two-arm randomized controlled trial, will compare the effect of adding core stabilization exercises to routine manual physical therapy in adults aged 40-60 years with moderate KOA. Group A will receive trunk stabilization exercises protocol along with knee routine manual physical therapy. Group B will be given only routine manual physical therapy protocol including manual mobilization, and routine knee strengthening. Outcomes will include NPRS for pain intensity, WOMAC for functional status and for balance during functional activities timed up and go test, stair climb test, 30 sec sit-to-stand test.

brief_summary:
1. Research background: Digital workflows integrating precise modeling, virtual design and computer-aided design/computer-aided manufacturing (CAD/CAM) fabrication have substantially improved restoration fit and clinical efficiency. Nevertheless, contemporary digital workflows still present limitations in occlusal reconstruction. Conventional CAD/CAM relies largely on static occlusal data points, which leads to mismatches between restorations and patients' actual functional mandibular pathways. Accordingly, dynamically guided occlusal reconstruction has become a key objective for enhancing the long-term stability and comfort of implant-supported rehabilitations. Particularly during the definitive restoration phase for edentulous patients, occlusal interactions between the implant superstructure and the opposing dentition exert a major influence on clinical chair time and patient satisfaction. Recently, high-precision digital mandibular motion analysis systems have emerged as effective solutions to address these challenges. Ultrasound-based mandibular tracking systems (e.g., Zebris JMA Optic) enable real-time capture of six-degrees-of-freedom mandibular movement and offer superior patient comfort compared with conventional electronic axiographic systems. Alternative technologies employ facial scanners to track spatial displacements of intraoral fiducial markers in real time. Meanwhile, facial scan data, dental cast scan data and CBCT data are registered and fused based on anterior dental anatomical landmarks, allowing direct visualization and recording of the true kinematic trajectories of the mandible and bilateral condyles on the three-dimensional CBCT model. This approach eliminates the need for a facebow or head-mounted apparatus and may provide improved comfort. The newly launched MetiSmile-MR/e-Motion platform by SHINING 3D acquires mandibular movement trajectories via the aforementioned multimodal data registration and fusion; however, its clinical performance in full-arch implant rehabilitation remains to be further validated.
2. Research objective: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of mandibular movement trajectories captured by two different digital technologies for dynamic occlusal design in maxillary full-arch implant rehabilitation. In addition, the potential benefits of these digitally recorded mandibular trajectories for dynamic occlusal design were assessed in terms of functional stability and patient satisfaction in full-arch implant rehabilitation, by examining mandibular pathways after definitive restoration delivery and patients' subjective comfort. Based on the above outcome measures, this study further evaluated whether the SHINING 3D multimodal data registration and fusion workflow could serve as an alternative to the electronic facebow for dynamic occlusal design in full-arch implant rehabilitation.
3. Study design and methods: Design type: prospective, interventional, single-center, randomized controlled non-inferiority study..Study duration: 2 years. Start time: From the date of adoption of ethics. End time: 2028. For all included patients, at the definitive impression stage, mandibular movement trajectories were captured using two different digital technologies. The trajectory datasets obtained from both digital approaches were imported into Exocad software for the design of definitive restorations. After the definitive restorations were inserted intraorally, panoramic radiographs were taken to confirm complete seating of the restorations. The restorations were three-dimensionally scanned with an intraoral scanner to generate pre-adjustment digital models. The total duration of occlusal adjustment was recorded as an indicator of clinical efficiency. Once satisfactory occlusion was achieved, the restorations were rescanned to acquire post-adjustment digital models. A one-month follow-up visit after definitive restoration delivery was arranged to evaluate the stability of mandibular movement trajectories captured by the different digital workflows.
interventions: the SHINING 3D intraoral scan-facial scan-CBCT fusion multimodal workflow
title: Clinical Outcomes of Digitally Recorded Mandibular Trajectories for Dynamic Occlusal Design in Full-Arch Implant Rehabilitation

brief_summary:
Patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation may develop alveolar derecruitment due to atelectasis, secretion retention, changes in body position, or acute respiratory distress syndrome. Lung recruitment maneuvers reopen partially collapsed alveoli by briefly increasing transpulmonary pressure, thereby improving lung volume and oxygenation; however, elevated airway pressure may also affect venous return, mean arterial pressure, and carbon dioxide elimination, and thus alter cerebral blood flow. Therefore, improved oxygenation does not necessarily indicate stable cerebral circulation.

At present, when selecting a lung recruitment modality in clinical practice, clinicians often rely on oxygenation response, respiratory mechanics, and operator experience, while dynamic observation of cerebral hemodynamics remains relatively insufficient. Recording only two time points before and after the maneuver may miss transient but clinically meaningful changes during pressurization, maintenance of high pressure, and recovery. Therefore, under controlled and safe conditions, it is necessary to use three commonly used clinical lung recruitment maneuvers as observational scenarios to describe cerebral hemodynamic changes during lung recruitment and to explore possible physiological factors in conjunction with cardiac output, systemic blood pressure, carbon dioxide, and respiratory mechanics. The findings are expected to provide a physiological basis for bedside cerebral perfusion monitoring and risk identification; however, short-term changes in Vm alone cannot prove that a particular maneuver is safer or improves long-term outcomes.
interventions: Method A: Incremental PEEP Recruitment Maneuver
primary_outcomes: mean flow velocity in the middle cerebral artery
title: Effects of Lung Recruitment on Cerebral Hemodynamics（LRCH）

brief_summary:
Breast cancer surgery, particularly modified radical mastectomy (MRM), can cause significant postoperative pain. Effective pain management is important to improve patient comfort, facilitate recovery, reduce opioid consumption, and potentially decrease the risk of persistent post-mastectomy pain.

This randomized controlled clinical trial aims to compare the effectiveness of ultrasound-guided subtransverse interligamentary (STIL) block and thoracic paravertebral block (PVB) for postoperative pain relief in female patients undergoing modified radical mastectomy.

Eligible patients will be randomly allocated into three groups: the STIL block group, the PVB group, and a control group receiving general anesthesia without a regional block. Both regional blocks will be performed under ultrasound guidance at the T4 thoracic level using 25 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine combined with 4 mg dexamethasone.

Postoperative pain will be assessed using a visual analogue scale (VAS) at rest and during movement. The study will also evaluate postoperative morphine consumption, time to first rescue analgesia, intraoperative fentanyl requirements, recovery characteristics, patient satisfaction, postoperative nausea and vomiting, and block-related complications.

The primary objective is to compare postoperative pain scores at rest 24 hours after surgery between patients receiving STIL block and those receiving PVB.

The findings may help determine whether STIL block provides an effective alternative to thoracic paravertebral block for postoperative analgesia following modified radical mastectomy.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain Score at Rest at 24 Hours
title: STIL Block Versus Paravertebral Block for Pain Relief After Modified Radical Mastectomy

brief_summary:
RSV-SHIELD: Study Summary

RSV-SHIELD is an investigator-initiated, prospective, single-centre, single-blind, Phase IV, randomised, placebo-controlled clinical trial designed to investigate the effects of passive immunoprophylaxis with clesrovimab, a long-acting monoclonal antibody against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), on nasopharyngeal pathogen carriage, respiratory microbial ecology, and local immune responses in infants.

The study aims to evaluate whether RSV prevention with clesrovimab influences not only RSV detection, viral load, and shedding dynamics but also the acquisition, persistence, and clearance of other respiratory viruses and bacterial pathogens. In addition, it will investigate changes in the nasopharyngeal microbiome and local inflammatory responses following immunoprophylaxis. These findings may provide novel insights into the interactions between RSV, other respiratory pathogens, and the developing respiratory microbiome, as well as the potential indirect effects of RSV immunoprophylaxis beyond the prevention of RSV-associated disease.

Approximately 162 healthy infants aged 0-12 months, born at a gestational age of at least 32 weeks, will be recruited at the Department of Paediatrics, University General Hospital of Heraklion, Crete, Greece. Eligible infants will fall within the approved age indication for clesrovimab but will not qualify for RSV monoclonal antibody prophylaxis under the current Greek National Immunisation Programme. Participants will be randomised in a 1:1 ratio to receive either a single intramuscular dose of clesrovimab (105 mg) or matching placebo (0.9% normal saline).

Participants will be followed for approximately eight months, with scheduled visits at baseline and months 1, 2, 3, and 5, an interim telephone assessment at month 4, and a final telephone follow-up at month 8. Additional visits will be conducted during episodes of acute respiratory tract infection.

Nasopharyngeal specimens will be collected longitudinally to assess RSV detection and viral load, other respiratory viruses, and bacterial colonisation, including Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, Staphylococcus aureus, and Streptococcus pyogenes. Nasopharyngeal microbiome composition and diversity will be investigated using 16S rRNA sequencing. Nasal lining fluid will also be collected to measure clesrovimab concentrations and local inflammatory biomarkers.

The primary objectives encompass RSV detection and shedding dynamics, non-RSV respiratory pathogen carriage and acquisition, and changes in the nasopharyngeal microbiome and inflammatory environment. Secondary outcomes include the incidence and clinical characteristics of respiratory tract infections, including bronchiolitis, pneumonia, acute otitis media, and wheezing episodes, as well as healthcare utilisation and hospitalisations. Adverse events and serious adverse events will be monitored throughout the study.

By combining a randomised controlled design with longitudinal molecular, microbiological, and immunological assessments, RSV-SHIELD seeks to generate evidence on the broader biological effects of RSV monoclonal antibody prophylaxis. The findings may contribute to a better understanding of respiratory pathogen interactions in early life and inform future RSV prevention strategies.

Approximately 3,400 characters, including spaces - within your 5,000-character limit.
primary_outcomes: To evaluate the effect of clesrovimab on nasopharyngeal RSV detection and viral shedding during the RSV season.
To evaluate the effect of clesrovimab on the detection of non-RSV respiratory viruses and the carriage/colonisation of respiratory bacterial pathogens in the nasopharynx.
To evaluate the effect of clesrovimab on the composition and dynamics of the nasopharyngeal microbiome and local inflammatory response.
title: Impact of Clesrovimab on Respiratory Pathogen Shedding in Infants: The RSV-SHIELD Trial

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is feasible, safe and tolerable when combined with standard rehabilitation after surgery to restore grasp in adults with tetraplegia caused by spinal cord injury. taVNS delivers gentle electrical stimulation through an electrode placed on the outer ear.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can participants follow the treatment schedule and complete the study assessments?
* Is the treatment well tolerated, and what side effects or medical problems occur?
* Are there preliminary differences in grasp function, tendon movement and daily activities between participants receiving active treatment and those receiving sham treatment?
* Does active treatment affect blood markers of inflammation and scar tissue formation? Researchers will compare active taVNS with sham treatment delivered using an identical device and a specially designed electrode that provides subtle sensory feedback without electrical stimulation. Both groups will receive the same standard postoperative rehabilitation. Approximately 40 adults undergoing surgical grasp reconstruction at the Center for Advanced Reconstruction of Extremities (CARE), Sahlgrenska University Hospital/Mölndal, Sweden, will be randomly assigned to the two groups in equal numbers. Participants, treating therapists and outcome assessors will not know which treatment participants receive.

Participants will:

* Use the assigned device with an electrode on the left outer ear for 60 minutes daily, starting during the week of surgery and continuing for three months.
* Receive training, together with a caregiver where needed, to use the device at home.
* Return for a five-day inpatient rehabilitation stay three weeks after surgery, during which treatment will be supervised.
* Complete assessments before surgery and at three weeks, 12 weeks, six months and 12 months after surgery.
* Complete tests of grasp function, grip and pinch strength, hand opening and movement, together with questionnaires about daily activities, independence, bowel function, mood and quality of life.
* Undergo ultrasound examinations to assess tendon movement and scar tissue around the tendons.
* Provide blood samples before and at several time points after surgery to investigate inflammation and tissue healing.
* Record each treatment session in a diary and report side effects or difficulties using the device.

Approximately 10-15 participants will also be invited to an interview about their experiences of treatment and rehabilitation around three months after surgery.

This feasibility study will help researchers plan a larger trial to determine whether adding taVNS to rehabilitation improves recovery after surgical grasp reconstruction.
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in grip function as assessed by Grasp and Release Test (GRT)
Incidence of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events [Safety and Tolerability]
title: taVNS and Rehabilitation After Grasp Reconstruction in Tetraplegia: A Randomized Feasibility Study

This study investigates whether a personalized, AI-supported digital education model can improve psychological outcomes and reduce planned cesarean preference.

brief_summary: The clinical study will involve the use of a dietary supplement based on the oral probiotic strain Streptococcus salivarius Evol12® in patients with head and neck cancer undergoing radiochemotherapy, with the aim of improving their quality of life. The hypothesis is that, as already outlined in scientific literature, modifying the oral microbiota through the use of the commensal S. salivarius, increasing its concentration and reducing the main pathogens in the oral cavity, may protect these patients and reduce the impact on their quality of life . A discovery of this kind would allow patients with head and neck cancer to be treated not only with standard therapy but also with treatments designed to modify the oral microbiota, which is not currently taken into consideration, in order to improve these patients' quality of life and compliance with treatment. Compared to the S. salivarius K12 strain, the S. salivarius eK12 (Evol12®) strain has a genome that is entirely similar to K12, but with a hypothetically greater antibacterial activity due to the presence of two specific genetic differences which allow for increased release of a bacteriocin: the salivabactin. Streptococcus salivarius eK12 (Evol12®) has undergone mutagenesis, acute toxicity, and subchronic toxicity studies in animals, conducted according to OECD guidelines by a GLPcertified laboratory, confirming its safety of use and absence of toxicity (In vitro and In vivo safety evaluation of Streptococcus salivarius eK12, a genetically modified dietary probiotic derived from the oral probiotic S. salivarius K12). In addition, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial conducted in healthy adults has been published, demonstrating its complete safety of use even at high dosages.
title: Streptococcus Salivarius Evol12® in Improving Quality of Life in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Cancer Treated With Radio(Chemo)Therapy: SMILE

The main outcome was the diameter of the biceps tendon measured by ultrasound four weeks after treatment started. The study also assessed shoulder pain, shoulder function, and difficulty using the arm at four weeks.

brief_summary:
This study evaluated how artificial intelligence (AI)-formatted clinical recommendations influence dental students' decisions about prescribing systemic antibiotics in endodontic cases.

In this randomized, three-arm, parallel-group, online experimental study, third-, fourth-, and fifth-year dental students in Türkiye were assigned to one of three conditions: a Control group receiving no AI recommendations, a Guideline-concordant AI group receiving recommendations consistent with established clinical guidance, or a Mixed-accuracy AI group receiving recommendations with varying levels of accuracy.

Participants evaluated ten hypothetical endodontic clinical scenarios and decided whether systemic antibiotic treatment was indicated. The primary outcome was the accuracy of antibiotic prescribing decisions compared with predefined reference decisions. Secondary outcomes included confidence in clinical decisions, trust in AI recommendations, agreement with recommendations, identification of potentially incorrect information, and inappropriate antibiotic prescribing patterns.

Data were collected between July 1 and July 6, 2026. A total of 328 participants were randomized, 318 met the eligibility criteria, and 271 completed all ten primary decision questions.
primary_outcomes: Accuracy of Systemic Antibiotic Prescribing Decisions
title: Effects of AI-Assisted Clinical Recommendations on Dental Students' Endodontic Antibiotic Prescribing Decisions

brief_summary:
This study is looking at a new way to start Sublocade, a monthly injectable medicine already approved in Canada for opioid use disorder. Right now, most people start Sublocade with two doses of 300 mg, one month apart. This study is testing a different, more gradual approach: a smaller dose (50 mg) on Day 1, a second small dose (50 mg) on Day 7, and then the regular dose (300 mg) on Day 14.

The study team wants to find out whether this gradual approach helps people transitioning from methadone, or people who have used buprenorphine before, get started on treatment more easily. Everyone in the study follows the same schedule, and no one gets a placebo (an inactive treatment).

Participants will get study visits on Day 1, Day 7, and Day 14, along with short daily check-ins about how they're feeling for about 4 weeks, and some questionnaires about their quality of life and treatment satisfaction. The study is being done at one clinic in Calgary, Alberta.
title: A Study of a New Induction and Dosing Schedule for Sublocade in Opioid Use Disorder
