title: Comparing the Plaque and Gingivitis Efficacy After Using a Stannous Fluoride Toothpaste or a Toothpaste in Conjunction With Dental Floss.

brief_summary:
Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is frequently associated with moderate-to-severe postoperative pain, substantial opioid consumption, and preoperative anxiety. Although spinal anesthesia is preferred for TKA, it does not provide prolonged analgesia after the block resolves.

This prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial aims to evaluate and compare the efficacy of perioperative oral mirogabalin versus melatonin versus placebo as opioid-sparing analgesic adjuncts in patients undergoing elective unilateral TKA under spinal anesthesia. The primary objective is to assess their impact on postoperative pain intensity and perioperative anxiety levels.
title: Mirogabalin vs. Melatonin for Pain and Anxiety After Total Knee Arthroplasty Under Spinal Anesthesia

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if insulin eye drops, added to standard care, can treat persistent corneal epithelial defects (PEDs) in adults age 18 and older. A PED is a corneal surface wound, at least 2 mm across, that has not healed after more than 14 days of standard treatment such as lubricants, antibiotic drops, or a bandage contact lens. The main question it aims to answer is:

\- Does adding insulin eye drops (1 IU/mL, four times daily) to standard care increase the proportion of eyes with complete corneal epithelial healing at 8 weeks?

The standard care plus insulin eye drops will be compared to standard care plus placebo eye drops (preservative-free saline) to see if insulin leads to more complete healing, faster healing, fewer recurrences, and better symptom relief. They will also assess the safety of the drops and their effects on corneal nerves.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned (1:1) to insulin or placebo drops. Neither participants nor the investigators assessing healing will know which drops are used. The study is single-center (Massachusetts Eye and Ear) and plans to enroll 40 participants, one eye each.
* Use the study drops four times daily for up to 8 weeks, along with standard care chosen by their cornea specialist, and return weekly for a fresh, refrigerated supply.
* Attend study visits at baseline and at weeks 1, 4, 8, and 12 for visual acuity testing, slit-lamp examination, fluorescein staining and photography of the defect, and imaging of corneal nerves (in vivo confocal microscopy).
* Complete symptom questionnaires (pain, foreign body sensation, light sensitivity) at baseline and week 8, and have corneal sensation tested before and after treatment.
* Have blood glucose monitored if they have diabetes.
primary_outcomes: Complete PED closure rate at 8 Weeks
title: Topical Insulin Therapy for Persistent Corneal Epithelial Defects

brief_summary:
This study will look at whether a monitoring method called near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS), can help assess lung disease in premature babies.

The main aim of this study is to describe lung oxygen levels measured by NIRS in premature babies with respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) during the first 72 hours after birth. The study will include babies born at or before 32 weeks of pregnancy who need continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) for RDS. The study will also assess whether these lung oxygen measurements can help predict which babies will need surfactant treatment, and whether they can predict which babies may need more than one dose of surfactant.

The study will also compare lung NIRS measurements with other ways of assessing breathing problems, including lung ultrasound scores and oxygen-related measurements. In addition, the researchers will compare lung oxygen measurements with brain oxygen measurements. They will also look at whether surfactant treatment changes oxygen levels in the lungs and brain. Information from routine vital signs, such as heart rate, breathing rate, and oxygen saturation, will also be studied to see whether these measurements can help predict the need for surfactant.

Added to this researchers will look at the hemodynamics of surfactant administration by seeing how the heart and blood vessels react to surfactant administration
title: Pulmonary Near-infrared Spectroscopy to Predict the Need for Surfactant in Very Low Birth Weight Infants

brief_summary:
When artificial intelligence (AI) recommends a treatment, clinicians must decide whether to follow it. This study tests whether showing the predicted consequences of a recommendation, in addition to the recommendation itself, helps clinicians accept appropriate advice and reject inappropriate advice.

We developed a clinician-anchored counterfactual model that compares the on-duty clinician's intravenous fluid and vasopressor plan with alternative plans for patients with sepsis. It predicts the patient's course under each plan and recommends a change only when the predicted benefit holds across several plausible assumptions about unrecorded factors; otherwise it states that the evidence is insufficient to recommend a change.

About 72 physicians from two hospitals, stratified by seniority, will review 30 retrospective, de-identified ICU decision points from patients with sepsis. In stage 1, each physician independently specifies fluid and vasopressor doses without any AI information. In stage 2, the same cases are reviewed under three conditions assigned by counterbalanced sequences: the case with the on-duty clinician's plan and no AI (B0); B0 plus the AI recommendation (B1); and B1 plus the predicted consequences of the on-duty and recommended plans (B2). The AI recommendation is identical in B1 and B2. Decision quality is assessed against plans made independently by expert intensivists. No patients are enrolled, and participants' decisions do not affect patient care.
primary_outcomes: Distance of final treatment decisions from the range of expert plans, B2 versus B1
title: AI Treatment Recommendations With Predicted Consequences for Sepsis Fluid and Vasopressor Decisions

brief_summary:
This single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy controlled trial aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of intraosseous versus intravenous flurbiprofen axetil for postoperative pain management in patients undergoing joint arthroplasty.

A total of 240 patients aged 65-80 years undergoing primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty, unicompartmental knee arthroplasty, total hip arthroplasty, or hemiarthroplasty will be enrolled. Participants will be stratified according to surgical procedure and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either intraosseous flurbiprofen axetil with intravenous saline placebo or intravenous flurbiprofen axetil with intraosseous saline placebo. The dose of flurbiprofen axetil will be 50 mg in both groups.

The primary outcome is postoperative pain intensity at rest, assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at predefined time points from 1 hour to 6 weeks after surgery. Secondary outcomes include pain during movement, cumulative opioid consumption within 72 hours, length of hospital stay, joint functional recovery, patient satisfaction, patient-controlled analgesia utilization, and adverse events.

This study aims to determine whether intraosseous administration of flurbiprofen axetil provides effective and safe postoperative analgesia compared with conventional intravenous administration following joint arthroplasty.
title: Intraosseous Injection of Flurbiprofen Axetil for Postoperative Analgesia in Joint Arthroplasty

brief_summary: The effects on physical fitness and wellbeing of being pupil at a certified Danish Sports School will be evaluated by YoYo Intermittent Recovery level 1 children's´ test, handgrib strength and KIDSCREEN-27
title: Evaluation of Sports School Certification in Denmark

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effect of a nursing intervention based on Orem's self-care theory on treatment burden and self-management among adolescents diagnosed with thalassemia. Adolescents with thalassemia face significant physical and psychosocial challenges that affect their daily routines and treatment adherence. The intervention consists of educational and supportive sessions designed to enhance self-care agency and reduce treatment burden. Participants will be evaluated before and after the implementation of the nursing program to measure changes in treatment burden and self-management behaviors.
title: Effect of Nursing Intervention on Treatment Burden and Self-management Among Adolescents With Thalassemia

brief_summary: This prospective study compared Bacillus clausii and Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG, each added to dietary management, with dietary management alone in children aged 12-48 months with functional constipation (Rome IV). Children assigned to probiotic treatment were randomly allocated to Bacillus clausii or Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (2 × 10⁹ spores or CFU daily for two months); consecutive children receiving dietary management alone served as controls. Defecation frequency, stool consistency, painful defecation and abdominal distension were assessed at baseline and at months 1 and 2.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of children with painful defecation
title: Bacillus Clausii or Lactobacillus Rhamnosus GG Added to Dietary Management in Young Children With Functional Constipation: a Prospective Comparative Study

brief_summary: Postoperative complications after oesophagectomy for cancer can worsen the short-term postoperative outcomes and the long-term survival. This study aims to compare the comprehensive complication index (CCI) and the commonly used Clavien-Dindo classification (CDC) in predicting postoperative outcomes after oesophagectomy for cancer.
primary_outcomes: Length of hospital stay in days
title: Does the Comprehensive Complication Index Add Value to the Clavien-Dindo Classification After Oesophagectomy for Cancer?

brief_summary: Sport-active adults face persistent stressors such as performance and body-related expectations, injury risk, training load, scheduling demands, and the challenge of balancing sport with work, caregiving, and other life commitments, all of which can undermine psychological well-being. These stressors can undermine psychological well-being, elevate perceived stress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms, and reduce overall satisfaction with sport performance. Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) has shown efficacy for emotional regulation, focus and body awareness, but traditional in-person MBSR can be inaccessible because of time, scheduling, geographic and stigma-related barriers. Chatbot-delivered interventions offer 24/7 accessibility, anonymity and personalised support. This project will adapt an existing chatbot-delivered MBSR programme, built with Power Virtual Agents on Microsoft Teams, to the context of sport-active adults, and will evaluate its feasibility, acceptability and preliminary efficacy in an eight-week, parallel-group, non-randomised controlled trial. Participants will be allocated non-randomly to either the intervention group or an educational control group. The intervention group will receive the eight-session chatbot-delivered MBSR programme (one session per week for eight weeks); the educational control group will receive mental health education messages via WhatsApp once weekly for eight weeks. Primary outcomes will be subjective sport performance satisfaction and psychological well-being; secondary outcomes will be depression, anxiety, perceived stress and mindfulness. Assessments will be conducted at baseline and immediately post-intervention.
interventions: An eight-week receive mental health education messages via WhatsApp
title: Chatbot-Delivered Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction Program for Sports Active Adults: Intervention Development and Feasibility Trial

brief_summary:
Xylitol is a natural sweetener that is widely used in chewing gum and oral care products because it helps prevent tooth decay. Some recent studies, mostly in older adults with heart disease or other health conditions, have raised questions about whether xylitol may affect blood clotting. It is not known whether regular, everyday amounts of xylitol have any effect on blood clotting in healthy young people.

This study will look at whether chewing xylitol gum every day for 4 weeks changes blood clotting tests in healthy adults aged 18 to 35 years. It will also look at whether xylitol gum changes the bacteria found in saliva.

Sixty healthy volunteers will be randomly assigned to one of two groups of 30 people each. One group will chew gum containing xylitol (2 pieces, 3 times a day, for a total of 6 grams of xylitol per day). The other group will chew gum that contains sorbitol instead of xylitol, in the same way and for the same length of time. Participants and researchers will know which gum is being used.

Blood and saliva samples will be collected at the start of the study and again after 4 weeks. The blood tests will measure platelet count, prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, fibrinogen, D-dimer, and thrombin-antithrombin complexes. The saliva samples will be used to study the types and amounts of bacteria in the mouth. Researchers will contact participants every week to ask how they are doing and to record any side effects.
primary_outcomes: Change in blood coagulation parameters following xylitol consumption
title: Effect of Xylitol Chewing Gum Consumption on Coagulation Parameters and Salivary Oral Microbiological Markers in Healthy Young Adults

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to determine whether a brief, objective cognitive assessment can detect exercise-induced changes in cognitive performance in adolescent athletes who have been medically cleared for return-to-play following sport-related concussion.
title: Cognitive Function in Athletes Cleared for Return-to-Play After Sport-Related Concussion

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether the hybrid ureteroenteric anastomosis technique reduces strictures (narrowing) at the junction between the ureters and the bowel compared with the standard Wallace and Bricker techniques in adults undergoing radical cystectomy with ileal conduit urinary diversion for bladder cancer.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the hybrid technique lower the rate of ureteroenteric stricture requiring an additional procedure within 12 months after surgery?
* Does the hybrid technique change postoperative complications, hydronephrosis (swelling of the kidney), kidney function, recovery of bowel function, length of hospital stay and quality of life?

Researchers will compare the hybrid technique with the Wallace and Bricker techniques to see which gives better early and late results.

Participants will:

* Undergo radical cystectomy with ileal conduit, with the ureters connected to the bowel using one of the three techniques
* Have routine blood tests before and after surgery
* Attend follow-up visits at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months after surgery for blood tests, kidney imaging and quality-of-life questionnaires

All tests are part of routine care; no additional study-specific tests are performed.
interventions: Wallace Ureteroenteric AnastomosisThe spatulated ureters are sutured together side-to-side to form a common plate, which is anastomosed end-to-end to the proximal end of the ileal conduit.
primary_outcomes: Rate of Ureteroenteric Anastomotic Stricture Requiring Intervention
title: Hybrid Versus Wallace and Bricker Ureteroenteric Anastomosis After Radical Cystectomy With Ileal Conduit

brief_summary: This study examines lower-limb muscle activation and smartphone-derived movement characteristics while 100 healthy university students complete five 2-minute walking conditions: forward gaze, downward gaze without a phone, passive smartphone viewing, smartphone texting, and smartphone voice recording. All participants will complete the conditions in the same fixed order, with a 2-minute seated passive-rest interval after each walking bout
interventions: Fixed-Sequence Gaze and Smartphone Tasks During Walking
primary_outcomes: Mean Bilateral Tibialis Anterior-Medial Gastrocnemius (TA-MG) Co-Contraction Index
title: Smartphone Use, EMG, and Walking Accelerometry

brief_summary: Prospective study evaluating the pharmacokinetics of colistin after IV administration of colistin different doses
primary_outcomes: 1. Evaluation of neonatal efficacy of different administered doses of IV colistin in neonatal sepsis. 2. Assessment of colistin related AKI rates in NICU. 3. Development of personalized approach for dose selection in neonatal sepsis
title: Colistin Use in Neonates ICU Patients With Gram Negative Resistant Infection

brief_summary: This is a first-in-human, multicentre, Phase 1, open-label study designed to evaluate the safety and tolerability of DAX-044 as monotherapy, and to determine its maximum tolerated dose, in adults with advanced solid tumours.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs) as Assessed by CTCAE v6.0
Maximum Tolerated Dose (MTD) of DAX-044 Based on Dose-Limiting Toxicities (DLTs) (Part 1)
title: DAX-044 in Adults With Advanced Solid Tumours: a First-in-human Study of Safety, Dose and Early Anti-cancer Activity.

brief_summary: This pilot randomized study examined how the color temperature of light affects emotional states and sleep in people with insomnia symptoms. Thirty participants with an Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) score of 8 or higher were randomly allocated to 500-lux light at 2700 K, 4000 K or 6500 K. After a 7-day baseline, participants received a daily 75-minute light exposure session at 17:00 for 7 days (15 minutes of dark adaptation followed by 60 minutes of light), followed by a 7-day follow-up. Insomnia severity, depression, anxiety and stress were assessed on days 1 and 21, and sleep was recorded with actigraphy and sleep logs.
title: Color Temperature of Light for Emotional States and Sleep in Insomnia

brief_summary:
This exploratory randomized controlled trial will test whether a short session of dry static apnoea (voluntary breath-holding while lying down, out of the water) helps trained breath-hold divers recover faster from a brief, standardized laboratory stressor than resting for the same amount of time.

Twenty-eight licensed breath-hold divers will attend a single afternoon session of about 85 minutes. All participants first complete the Maastricht Acute Stress Test (alternating immersion of one hand in cold water at about 2 °C with mental arithmetic and negative feedback). They are then randomly assigned to one of two 24-minute conditions: four supervised dry static apnoeas at 50% of their personal best (maximum 3 minutes each), or lying at rest while listening to a neutral informative audio. Both groups then rest until 60 minutes after the start of the stressor.

The main outcome is salivary cortisol 60 minutes after the start of the stressor. Heart rate, heart rate variability, blood pressure, state anxiety and perceived stress will also be compared between groups.
primary_outcomes: Salivary cortisol 60 minutes after stressor onset (S4)
title: Dry Static Apnoea for Recovery From Acute Laboratory Stress in Trained Breath-Hold Divers

brief_summary:
Peri-implant diseases are inflammatory conditions affecting the tissues surrounding dental implants. Peri-implant mucositis involves inflammation of the soft tissues, whereas peri-implantitis is characterized by inflammation accompanied by progressive supporting bone loss. Hormonal, metabolic, and inflammatory changes associated with menopause may influence peri-implant tissue health.

This observational, cross-sectional study aims to investigate the associations of serum homocysteine, vitamin B12, folate, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, and the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) with peri-implant health and disease status in postmenopausal women.

Approximately 120 postmenopausal women aged 45-70 years with at least one functional dental implant will be included. Participants will be classified into three groups based on clinical and radiographic examinations: peri-implant health, peri-implant mucositis, and peri-implantitis.

Blood samples will be collected to measure homocysteine, vitamin B12, folate, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH). FSH will be used to support the assessment of postmenopausal status. The SII will be calculated from neutrophil, lymphocyte, and platelet counts obtained from complete blood count measurements.

Periodontal and peri-implant risk profiles will be evaluated using Periodontal Risk Assessment (PRA) and Implant Disease Risk Assessment (IDRA). Associations between systemic biomarkers, clinical and radiographic parameters, and individual risk profiles will be statistically analyzed.

The findings may contribute to a better understanding of the systemic metabolic and inflammatory characteristics associated with peri-implant diseases in postmenopausal women and provide preliminary data for future longitudinal studies.
title: Systemic Inflammatory and Metabolic Biomarkers of Peri-Implant Diseases in Postmenopausal Women

brief_summary:
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) in childhood is a significant burden and reduces the quality of life for both children and their parents. CKD is especially burdensome when it progresses to end stage kidney disease (ESKD, previously referred to as end-stage renal disease or ESRD), placing considerable demands on a childs entire family. Although studies are available for all-cause CKD and for some disease subsets, there is no study capturing quality of life in children or adolescents specifically affected by autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD). These children are often severely affected prenatally and postnatally have problems due to massive kidney enlargement, hypertension, kidney failure, and portal hypertension. They often need to receive kidney replacement therapy during childhood.

The need to include patients and their lived experience in the design of clinical trials exists for all diseases, but is implemented infrequently, especially in the field of rare diseases. The negative consequences of limited patient/parent input in clinical trial design for rare diseases has been recently highlighted by a report from the International Rare Diseases Research Consortium (IRDiRC).
primary_outcomes: ULQIE (Ulm Quality of Life Inventory for Parents of Chronically Ill Children)
title: Capturing Quality of Life and Priorities for Clinical Research in Parents and Patients With Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease

brief_summary: Medical students often encounter significant stressors and challenges that, over time, can impact their academic performance and professional lives by diminishing psychological resilience and well-being, eventually leading to mental health issues and neurotic disorders. This is largely due to the demanding nature and responsibilities of medical school. Consequently, multiple studies have been conducted to identify prevention programs that can help students cope with these challenges. Although various behavioral therapy-based prevention and coping mechanisms have been proposed in the general population, few studies have specifically applied these programs to medical students, highlighting the need for further research in this group.
title: Mindfulness-based Intervention to Improve Psychological Resilience and Wellbeing on Medical Students

brief_summary:
This study utilized a laboratory-based, mixed-model repeated measures design (2 groups × 2 time points) to investigate the habitual and acute effects of smartphone sitting posture on hip internal rotation range of motion (ROM) and piriformis pressure pain threshold (PPT).

A total of 50 participants were classified into either a Sacral Sitting Group or a Neutral Sitting Group based on a questionnaires, direct observation, and electronic digital inclinometer assessment. During initial screening, participants used their smartphones in their natural, habitual sitting posture without postural correction.

Following baseline assessments of hip internal rotation ROM and piriformis PPT (pre-test), all participants underwent a standardized 30-minute exposure session, during which they were instructed to maintain a sacral sitting posture while using a smartphone.

During the session, postural alignment was monitored to ensure that participants maintained a consistent sacral sitting posture. Posterior pelvic tilt angles (measured at the S2 level) and trunk flexion angles (measured over the lower thoracolumbar region) were measured using an electronic digital inclinometer at 0, 15, and 30 minutes.

Participants were permitted to perform low-movement smartphone activities, such as scrolling or browsing social media, while activities requiring substantial body movement were not permitted.

Immediately after the session, hip internal rotation ROM and piriformis PPT were reassessed (post-test), and the FAIR test was performed to evaluate acute symptom reproduction. The study examined within-participant changes and compared these changes between the two habitual sitting groups.
primary_outcomes: Change in Hip Internal Rotation Range of Motion (ROM)
Change in Piriformis Muscle Pressure Pain Threshold (PPT)
title: Acute Effects of Sacral Sitting Posture Using Smartphone on Hip Internal Rotation and Piriformis Pressure Pain Threshold

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, multicenter, randomized, controlled Phase 2 clinical study to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of adding serplulimab (an immunotherapy drug that targets PD-1) to standard second-line treatment with bevacizumab and chemotherapy. The study enrolls adult patients with advanced or metastatic, left-sided colorectal cancer whose tumors are microsatellite stable (MSS) or mismatch repair proficient (pMMR) and carry no mutations in the KRAS, NRAS, or BRAF genes (wild-type), and whose cancer worsened after first-line treatment containing an anti-EGFR antibody and chemotherapy.

Approximately 96 eligible participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to one of two treatment groups. Participants in the experimental group (Arm A) will receive serplulimab plus bevacizumab and chemotherapy every 3 weeks, while participants in the control group (Arm B) will receive bevacizumab and chemotherapy every 3 weeks. In both groups, the chemotherapy regimen is chosen based on prior first-line therapy: participants who previously received irinotecan will receive CapeOX (oxaliplatin and capecitabine), and those who previously received oxaliplatin will receive mXELIRI (irinotecan and capecitabine). Treatment will continue until disease progression, unacceptable side effects, withdrawal of consent, or study completion.
title: Serplulimab Plus Bevacizumab and Chemotherapy for Left-Sided, KRAS/NRAS/BRAF Wild-Type Colorectal Cancer After First-Line Anti-EGFR Therapy

brief_summary: Participants are randomized into two groups: gait retraining and habitual walking. In the gait retraining group, an intervention consisting of 10 training sessions on a treadmill aims to reduce medial tibiofemoral joint loading during walking. Real-time visual biofeedback on a knee joint loading metric is provided during some of the training sessions to facilitate learning. The habitual walking group participates in an equal number of training sessions where they perform their habitual walking and do not try to change their walking technique. Changes in knee joint cartilage properties are assessed at 5 months.
title: Personalized Gait Retraining to Support Knee Health in Older Adults

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether individually tailored balance training based on the STABLE approach (Specific Training According to BaLance Evaluation) prevents falls better than the Otago Exercise Program in older adults with impaired balance. STABLE uses five simple clinical tests to build a balance profile, from which a physical therapist selects a few home exercises aimed at the person's main balance problems. The main question it aims to answer is: Does STABLE reduce the proportion of participants who fall at least once during the 26 weeks after the training period, compared with the Otago Exercise Program? Researchers will also compare number of falls, injurious falls, hospital admissions, mortality, balance and gait performance, fear of falling, dizziness, physical activity and quality of life.

Participants will:

* be randomized to STABLE or to the Otago Exercise Program (supplemented with gaze stabilization exercises if they have vestibular dysfunction)
* perform supervised home exercises for 3 to 4 months with 2 to 6 follow-up physical therapy consultations at the hospital or in their municipal rehabilitation center
* complete a balance and gait test before and after the training period, measured with a body-worn movement sensor and a force plate
* answer a short text message (SMS) questionnaire about falls once a week for 26 weeks after the training period Hospital admissions and mortality are collected from medical records 6 and again 24 months after the end of training. Participants' and physical therapists' experiences of the two approaches are explored in qualitative interviews.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants who fall at least once
title: Individually Tailored Balance Training for Older Adults at Risk of Falling

brief_summary: The OASIS study aims to identify and characterize circulating molecular signatures associated with ovarian aging, and to determine how these signatures relate to multidomain healthspan during the menopausal transition. The study consists of three parts. Part 1 is a retrospective analysis of existing clinical data and stored biospecimens from approximately 500 women aged 50-85 years. Part 2 is a prospective cohort of 300 women aged 40-50 years who will undergo comprehensive clinical, gynecological, and molecular assessments over 24 months, followed by individualized medical management based on their clinical findings. Part 3 (PRISM) is a nested substudy involving up to 30 women from the prospective cohort who will undergo intensive hormonal and ultrasound monitoring across a single menstrual cycle.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with abnormal ovarian or adnexal ultrasound findings
Within-woman changes in reproductive endocrine measures
title: OvariAn Secretome and Integrated HealthSpan

brief_summary:
The main objective of this project is to conduct a multicentre, prospective, randomised, controlled clinical trial to evaluate the clinical value of tranexamic acid in patients undergoing mastoidectomy. The study population consists of patients with chronic suppurative otitis media scheduled to undergo mastoidectomy. They will be randomised in a 1:1 ratio to either the pre-operative intravenous tranexamic acid group or the saline control group; both groups will undergo treatment in accordance with standardised anaesthesia and surgical protocols. The main research components include:

1. Evaluation of the dry ear rate: The primary outcome measure was to compare the difference in dry ear rates between the two groups one month post-operatively, in order to verify the effect of tranexamic acid on improving the dry ear rate following mastoidectomy. The assessment of the dry ear rate was carried out by an ENT specialist unaware of the study group allocation via clinical otoscopic examination; a dry ear was defined as the absence of discharge in the ear canal and complete epithelialisation of the mastoid surgical site. The assessment time point for the primary outcome measure was one month post-operatively.
2. Postoperative hearing assessment: This will be assessed based on the improvement in hearing at 3 months postoperatively compared with preoperative levels.
3. Safety assessment: The safety assessment will primarily include common adverse reactions associated with the use of tranexamic acid (e.g. nausea, vomiting, dizziness) and serious adverse events (e.g. venous thromboembolism, myocardial infarction, epileptic seizures). These will be comprehensively evaluated in conjunction with clinical signs and laboratory tests to ensure the safety and feasibility of the intervention.

Through this study, the project aims to determine whether tranexamic acid can effectively reduce the incidence of dry ear in the early postoperative period following mastoidectomy, and to provide evidence-based support for its clinical implementation.
title: Tranexamic Acid for Recovery After Modified Radical Mastoidectomy in Patients With Chronic Suppurative Otitis Media

brief_summary: This study is a six-arm individually randomized group-treated (IRGT) trial comparing five16-week standalone flourishing curricula conditions with a control condition consisting of the regular curriculum. Participants will be individually randomized to one of the six conditions. Self-report variables and heart rate variability (HRV) data will be assessed at four time points: T1 (baseline, before the curriculum begins), T2 (8-week midterm), T3 (16-week, at the end of the curriculum), and T4 (beginning of next term), with the main outcome testing changes between T1 and T3. Primary outcomes include the lnRMSSD as a measure of HRV and the overall self-reported flourishing score. Secondary outcomes include 20 domain specific psychological scales and two other HRV measures (SDNN, and mean heart rate). Course-specific knowledge tests will also be administered to gauge participant engagement and course effectiveness. Study results will be reported in accordance with the Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials (CONSORT) guidelines for non-pharmacological interventions.
lead_sponsor: Universidad del Sinú - Elías Bechara Zainúm
title: Flourishing for Peace

brief_summary: The aim of this clinical study is to evaluate the outcomes of surgical treatment of morbid obesity using a combined approach involving a modified laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy technique and botulinum toxin.
interventions: Modified anti-reflux laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy with posterior cruroplasty and Toupet (270° posterior) fundoplication
A modified anti-reflux laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy technique combined with endoscopic injection of botulinum toxin into the pyloric sphincter
lead_sponsor: West Kazakhstan Marat Ospanov Medical University
primary_outcomes: Incidence of postoperative gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)
title: Modified Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy With the Use of Botulinum Toxin for the Prevention of Postoperative Gastroesophageal Reflux in Patients With Morbid Obesity.

brief_summary:
Physiologic gingival melanin hyperpigmentation, although clinically benign, frequently represents a significant esthetic concern for individuals with excessive gingival display or a high lip line. Surgical scalpel de-epithelization is the traditional gold-standard technique for removing pigmented gingival tissue, yet it is associated with intraoperative hemorrhage, postoperative pain, and healing by secondary intention. Non-surgical intramucosal mesotherapy using glutathione-a potent endogenous tripeptide antioxidant that inhibits tyrosinase activity and shifts melanin synthesis toward lighter pheomelanin-has been proposed as a minimally invasive alternative.

The objective of this prospective, parallel-group, two-arm randomized controlled clinical trial was to compare patient esthetic satisfaction, objective pigmentation intensity (Dummett-Gupta Oral Pigmentation Index \[DOPI\]) and extent (Takashi Melanin Pigmentation Index \[MPI\]), postoperative pain (Visual Analogue Scale \[VAS\]), soft-tissue wound healing (Landry Wound Healing Index), and first-day postoperative bleeding between non-surgical intra-gingival glutathione injection and conventional surgical scalpel scraping over a 6-month follow-up period.
primary_outcomes: Change in Gingival Pigmentation Intensity Assessed by the Dummett-Gupta Oral Pigmentation Index (DOPI)
Change in Gingival Pigmentation Extent Assessed by the Takashi Melanin Pigmentation Index (MPI)
Patient Esthetic Satisfaction and Treatment Acceptability Questionnaire
title: Gingival Depigmentation Using Intra-Gingival Glutathione Injection Versus Surgical Scalpel Scraping

brief_summary:
This study will examine whether ultrasound guidance during laparoscopic surgery can help surgeons remove uterine fibroids more completely. Uterine fibroids are noncancerous growths in the womb (uterus). Small fibroids or those deep in the uterine wall may be difficult to identify during surgery. Laparoscopic ultrasound uses a probe inside the abdomen to provide images of the uterus during the operation.

The study plans to enroll 110 premenopausal women aged 20 to 50 who have multiple uterine fibroids, need surgery, and wish to keep their uterus. Participants will be assigned by chance to laparoscopic ultrasound-guided myomectomy or conventional laparoscopic myomectomy, with 55 participants planned for each group. Myomectomy is surgery to remove fibroids while preserving the uterus.

The main outcome is the percentage of fibroids removed. For each participant, this is calculated by dividing the number of fibroids removed during surgery by the total number removed plus the number remaining on postoperative imaging, and multiplying by 100. Remaining fibroids will be assessed by transvaginal ultrasound or pelvic magnetic resonance imaging within 3 months after surgery.

Researchers will also assess the percentage of participants with remaining fibroids at 3 months, the difference between the number of fibroids removed and the number identified before surgery, surgical safety, postoperative recovery, and questionnaire scores related to sexual function, disability, anxiety, and quality of recovery. Follow-up visits are scheduled at 1, 3, and 12 months after surgery.
title: Laparoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Removal of Multiple Uterine Fibroids

brief_summary:
Patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) require septal reduction therapy to relieve left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO). Septal myectomy is an open surgical procedure that resects hypertrophied septal myocardium to reduce outflow tract obstruction. However, it is associated with relatively substantial trauma. Some patients cannot tolerate surgery due to comorbidities or decline open-chest surgery.

Transcoronary alcohol ablation is a classic minimally invasive septal reduction therapy with a clinical history of nearly 30 years. Alcohol ablation induces myocardial injury via a chemical agent to reduce septal hypertrophy, widen the left ventricular outflow tract, lower the systolic pressure gradient, and improve clinical symptoms. It serves as a minimally invasive alternative to surgery. Nevertheless, the efficacy of this technique is highly dependent on the anatomical features of septal branches. Suboptimal outcomes may occur in some patients owing to variable septal branch anatomy. In addition, due to the high myocardial permeability of alcohol, atrioventricular block occurs in approximately 20% of patients after the procedure.

In recent years, transcoronary radiofrequency ablation has emerged as a novel minimally invasive septal reduction approach in clinical practice. For radiofrequency ablation, a microcatheter is advanced over a coronary guidewire into the septal branch. The proximal end of the guidewire is connected to a radiofrequency ablation generator, and myocardial ablation is delivered around the guidewire tip. Occlusion of the septal branch may further potentiate the ablative effect. This technique is less limited by anatomical variations of septal branches, features a shorter learning curve, and may have less impact on the conduction system. Compared with alcohol ablation, it enables more precise ablation with potentially superior safety. Both minimally invasive strategies achieve an obstruction relief rate exceeding 90%. To date, head-to-head data comparing the efficacy and safety profiles of these two minimally invasive therapies remain absent. Therefore, this randomized controlled trial is designed to compare the efficacy and safety of transcoronary alcohol ablation versus transcoronary radiofrequency ablation for hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy.

You will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to either the transcoronary alcohol ablation group or the transcoronary radiofrequency ablation group using a block randomization schedule. The probability of assignment to either group is 50%.

After randomization, cardiopulmonary exercise testing data, laboratory results and echocardiographic data will be collected at baseline, and the impact of cardiomyopathy on your quality of life will be assessed. Procedures in both groups will be performed by designated operators of the study team following standardized protocols. You will be blinded to the assigned treatment. In both groups, SonoVue will be injected into the coronary septal branch intraoperatively, and transthoracic echocardiography will be used to confirm that the ablation target is the critical site responsible for obstruction to ensure precise treatment. In the alcohol ablation group, 2-3 mL of absolute alcohol will be injected into the septal branch. In the radiofrequency ablation group, the guidewire will be connected to the radiofrequency generator; ablation energy will be set at 30-40 W, with 3 ablation applications of 30 seconds each at a single target site. Intraoperative electrocardiogram, heart rate, blood pressure and symptoms will be closely monitored, and the pressure gradient will be measured in real time using catheters and ultrasound. All patients will receive standardized medical therapy after the procedure. You will attend an outpatient follow-up visit at 3 months post-procedure, where repeat cardiopulmonary exercise testing, laboratory tests and echocardiography will be performed, and the post-procedure impact of cardiomyopathy on your quality of life will be re-evaluated. The primary endpoint of this study is the improvement in peak oxygen consumption on cardiopulmonary exercise testing at 3 months after treatment. No blood or tissue samples will be collected or stored for this study.
primary_outcomes: ncidence of new-onset complete left or right bundle branch block and/or permanent pacemaker implantation
title: A Single-Center, Randomized Controlled Trial of Transcoronary Radiofrequency Ablation Versus Transcoronary Alcohol Ablation for Hypertrophic Obstructive Cardiomyopathy

brief_summary:
SSpasticity is a common motor disorder following central nervous system injury, characterized by a velocity-dependent increase in muscle tone. It affects diverse populations, including patients with stroke, spinal cord injury, multiple sclerosis, or cerebral palsy, and leads to significant functional, pain-related, and medico-economic consequences.

Clinical assessment currently relies on the Modified Tardieu Scale (MTS) and the Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS), whose main limitations are low inter- and intra-rater reproducibility and subjective quantification. Coupling inertial measurement units (IMU) with a portable dynamometer represents a promising instrumental approach to overcome these limitations.

The hypothesis of this pilot clinical investigation is that instrumental measurement combining a portable dynamometer and inertial sensors would achieve satisfactory inter- and intra-rater reproducibility for the assessment of elbow flexor spasticity in patients with unilateral spastic paresis, thereby offering a reliable and objective alternative to current clinical scales.

This project proposes an instrumental assessment of upper-limb spasticity simultaneously combining kinematic measurement (angle, angular velocity) via two K-Move inertial sensors and measurement of resistance force via the K-Push dynamometer (Kinvent, Montpellier), which can easily be used during consultations or at the patient's bedside. This clinical investigation will secondarily assess the feasibility of a kinematic analysis based exclusively on videos acquired by tablet during the instrumental assessment.
primary_outcomes: Inter-rater and intra-rater reproducibility of instrumental measurement for elbow flexor spasticity assessment
title: Evaluation of the Reliability of a Wearable Device Combining Inertial Sensors and a Dynamometer for Analyzing Elbow Flexor Spasticity in Patients With Hemiplegia

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether adding an HA380 hemoadsorption cartridge to continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) helps adults with septic shock and acute kidney injury requiring CRRT recover from shock better than CRRT alone. Septic shock is a life-threatening condition in which an infection triggers an excessive inflammatory response, causing very low blood pressure and organ failure. The HA380 cartridge is a device placed in the CRRT blood circuit that is designed to remove inflammatory molecules (cytokines) from the blood.

The main question it aims to answer is: Does CRRT combined with the HA380 cartridge result in a lower blood lactate level (a marker of poor oxygen delivery to the body's tissues) at 24 hours than CRRT alone? Researchers will also compare the two groups in terms of the amount of blood-pressure-supporting medicines needed, blood levels of inflammatory cytokines, organ function, time to recovery from shock, need for organ support, length of intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital stay, survival up to 28 days, and side effects.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to receive either CRRT combined with the HA380 cartridge or CRRT alone, in addition to the same standard septic shock care
* If assigned to the HA380 group, receive three HA380 cartridges consecutively, each for 6 hours (18 hours in total), followed by CRRT alone as needed
* Have their vital signs, medicine doses and blood tests recorded before treatment and at set times up to day 7
* Be followed up for survival and recovery until day 28
primary_outcomes: Arterial Blood Lactate Concentration at 24 Hours
title: HA380 Hemoadsorption Combined With Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy Versus Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy Alone in Septic Shock

brief_summary:
Current DNA sequencing capabilities and the recent and ongoing advances in molecular diagnosis of genetic diseases through genomic technologies are opening up new application opportunities in public health that were previously unattainable. This project aims to concretely assess the sustainability and feasibility of neonatal genomic screening designed to identify individuals carrying genetic diseases with neonatal or infant onset. It also seeks to explore the expectations of stakeholders and the public, to define the experimental diagnostic pathway using Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS), to analytically consider the bioethical aspects at various stages, and to evaluate the health implications of the screening process.

Neonatal screening offers significant advantages in terms of early diagnosis of congenital diseases, which is crucial for initiating therapy as soon as possible to prevent or reduce serious health consequences for the newborn, thereby significantly improving prognosis. Moreover, early diagnosis can avoid the "diagnostic odyssey" that often affects families of children suspected of having a genetic disease-an ordeal that in some cases can last for years, consuming time, energy, and financial resources, and causing substantial psychological strain.

Currently, based on Resolution of Regione Lombardia No. XI / 111 of14/05/2018, biochemical screening for around forty endocrine and metabolic diseases is available in Lombardy. This is performed using a few drops of blood taken from the newborn's heel in the first days after birth. Genetic screening would allow for an expanded analysis including several hundred genes responsible for neonatal or typically pediatric-onset monogenic diseases, potentially covering all known monogenic diseases and specific gene variants that influence pharmacogenetic sensitivity. Furthermore, identifying the genetic defect in the child would enable targeted family-level counseling to calculate recurrence risk and evaluate possible alternatives (e.g., prenatal diagnosis, pre-implantation diagnosis).

The feasibility study we propose, in addition to the specific investigations required by the call, aims to evaluate whether whole genome sequencing (WGS) could be a cost-effective strategy in a neonatal screening context where early and pre-symptomatic diagnosis may offer clinical benefits to the newborn and their family.
conditions: This is a Genomics Newborn Screening Study
interventions: genomic analyses through bot WES and WGS
title: Neonatal Genomic Screening: Feasibility, Expectations, Definition of the Diagnostic Pathway, and Implications for Public Health

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the effects of a MIND diet-based nutritional intervention on brain fog, perceived stress, sleep quality, and selected biochemical parameters in young adults. It will also compare the effects of the MIND diet with those of the Mediterranean diet and usual dietary habits.

The MIND diet (Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay) is a dietary pattern that combines elements of the Mediterranean and DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) diets. It emphasizes the consumption of green leafy vegetables, other vegetables, berries, nuts, whole grains, legumes, fish, poultry, and olive oil, while limiting foods high in saturated fat, processed foods, and sweets. The Mediterranean diet similarly emphasizes plant-based foods, olive oil, whole grains, legumes, vegetables, fruits, nuts, and fish.

Young adults aged 18-35 years who meet the study eligibility criteria will be included. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: a MIND diet intervention group, a Mediterranean diet intervention group, or a control group.

Participants in the MIND diet group will receive nutritional guidance and follow a MIND diet-based dietary plan for 12 weeks. Participants in the Mediterranean diet group will receive nutritional guidance and follow a Mediterranean diet-based dietary plan for the same period. Participants in the control group will continue their usual dietary habits without receiving a structured dietary intervention during the study period.

Assessments will be conducted at baseline and at the end of the 12-week intervention. These assessments will include brain fog, perceived stress, sleep quality, dietary intake, and anthropometric measurements. Brain fog, perceived stress, and sleep quality will be evaluated using standardized assessment questionnaires. Dietary intake and adherence to the assigned dietary patterns will also be monitored throughout the intervention.

Selected biochemical parameters, including fasting blood glucose, total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, triglycerides, liver enzymes, uric acid, urea, and creatinine, will be assessed through blood samples.

The study will investigate whether following the MIND or Mediterranean dietary pattern for 12 weeks is associated with changes in brain fog, perceived stress, sleep quality, and selected biochemical parameters in young adults. The findings may contribute to a better understanding of the relationship between dietary patterns and cognitive, psychological, sleep-related, and metabolic health.
primary_outcomes: Change in Brain Fog Scale Score
title: Effects of MIND Diet on Brain Fog, Stress, and Sleep Quality in Young Adults

brief_summary:
Detailed Description:

Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome (PFPS) is one of the most frequent causes of anterior knee pain in clinical practice. It is primarily caused by mechanical dysfunctions and muscular imbalances between the patella and the femur, particularly involving weak quadriceps and hip stabilizing muscles.

Currently, supervised closed kinetic chain exercises targeting the knee and hip are considered standard conservative therapy due to their long-term effectiveness in stabilizing joint mechanics. High-intensity magnetic therapy is an innovative, non-invasive physical therapy modality that applies pulsed magnetic fields at a short distance (approximately 1 cm from the knee) to manage acute and chronic musculoskeletal pain. However, scientific evidence regarding the added clinical benefits of high-intensity magnetic therapy when combined with exercise for patellofemoral pain remains limited.

Study Hypothesis:

Combining high-intensity magnetic therapy with closed kinetic chain exercises for the knee and hip will produce greater improvements in knee pain reduction and functional recovery than closed kinetic chain exercises alone in patients with patellofemoral chondropathy.

Study Design and Interventions:

This randomized intervention study includes adult male and female participants with a clinical and radiological diagnosis of patellofemoral chondropathy.

To participate in the study, all candidate participants must fulfill all specified eligibility and inclusion criteria and provide signed written informed consent prior to enrollment.

Participants are randomly assigned in a treatment groups:

Group 1 (Exercise Alone): Participants complete 20 daily treatment sessions (Monday through Friday) consisting of supervised closed kinetic chain exercises designed to strengthen the stabilizing muscles of the knee and hip joint. Exercises consist of 10 repetitions per exercise during the first 10 sessions, increasing to 2 sets of 10 repetitions for the remaining 10 sessions.

Group 2 (High-Intensity Magnetic Therapy + Exercise): Participants receive 15 minutes of non-invasive high-intensity magnetic therapy applied to the knee (frequency: 3-15 Hz; intensity: 75-100% adapted to individual pain threshold) immediately followed by the exact same exercise protocol as Group 1.

Evaluations and Outcomes:

Participant assessments take place at three time points: baseline (prior to intervention), post-treatment (immediately following session 20), and at 1-month follow-up. The primary outcome is pain. Secondary outcomes include physical activity levels, sleep quality, knee joint range of motion, thigh muscle circumference, Body Mass Index (BMI), and anatomical patellofemoral measurements.
title: A Randomized Controlled Trial Comparing Repetitive Peripheral Magnetic Stimulation and Exercise in Adults With Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome.

brief_summary:
The purpose of this clinical study is to evaluate how well the lumetry device performs in two areas: estimating the level of carbon dioxide in the arterial blood (paCO2) and screening for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

lumetry is a small handheld device that analyzes exhaled breath. Participants breathe normally into the device for 60 seconds. No forced or maximal breathing maneuvers are required for the lumetry measurement.

Today, the carbon dioxide level in the blood is usually measured with a blood gas analysis, which requires a blood sample. COPD is usually diagnosed with spirometry, a lung function test that requires maximal breathing effort and trained staff.

In this study, adults with COPD of different severity and adults without known lung disease each attend a single study visit. All participants perform one lumetry breath measurement and a standard lung function test (forced spirometry). Participants with COPD also give a small capillary blood sample from the earlobe for blood gas analysis, and some of them additionally have their carbon dioxide level measured through the skin (transcutaneous measurement). By comparing the lumetry results with these established methods, the study assesses how accurately the device estimates the carbon dioxide level in the blood. By comparing the lumetry COPD screening result with spirometry and the confirmed clinical diagnosis, the study assesses how reliably the device distinguishes between people with and without COPD.

The study is conducted at one hospital in Vienna, Austria, and will include 300 participants.
primary_outcomes: Difference in Mean Absolute Deviation From Blood Gas paCO2 Between lumetry-Estimated paCO2 and End-Tidal Carbon Dioxide (petCO2)
Sensitivity of the lumetry COPD Screening Result
Specificity of the lumetry COPD Screening Result
title: Performance of Lumetry for Arterial Carbon Dioxide (paCO2) Assessment and Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) Screening

Does adding an iPACK block to a femoral triangle block lower postoperative pain scores over the first 48 hours? Does the combined block reduce the amount of opioid pain medication needed and delay the time to first rescue pain medication? Does the combined block improve early knee function (quadriceps strength, knee range of motion, and patient-reported knee scores) without causing muscle weakness or other complications?

Researchers will compare a femoral triangle block plus an iPACK block to a femoral triangle block alone (with a sham procedure to keep patients unaware of their group) to see if the added iPACK block provides better pain relief and recovery after ACL reconstruction.

Participants will:

Receive either a femoral triangle block plus an iPACK block, or a femoral triangle block alone, under ultrasound guidance before or after surgery Rate their pain at rest and during movement at 6, 12, 24, and 48 hours after surgery Have their pain medication use, quadriceps strength, knee movement, and time to first walking recorded during the hospital stay Complete knee function questionnaires (IKDC, Lysholm, and KOOS) before surgery and at follow-up visits at 2 weeks, 6 weeks, and 3 months Be monitored for side effects such as nausea, vomiting, falls, and nerve-related problems

brief_summary:
FAITH-T1D/1, exploratory, Phase I, open-label, non-randomized, single-arm, multicenter clinical trial designed to evaluate the dose-dependent effects of tirzepatide on gastric emptying in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) and overweight or obesity.

The study will investigate tirzepatide administered once weekly as an adjunct to participants' usual insulin therapy delivered through automated insulin delivery (AID) systems. Tirzepatide will be administered subcutaneously, with gradual dose escalation from 2.5 mg up to 15 mg at four-week intervals, according to clinical tolerability and the protocol-defined dosing schedule. Its use in this population is off-label.

The study follows a longitudinal, within-subject design in which each participant serves as their own control. Gastric emptying will be assessed by gastric emptying scintigraphy using a standardized solid meal at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, 16 and 24. The primary objective is to characterize changes in gastric emptying in relation to tirzepatide dose. Secondary and exploratory objectives include evaluating metabolic and glycemic parameters, gastrointestinal symptoms, postprandial glucagon, lipidomic and metabolomic profiles, and the safety and tolerability of treatment. Continuous glucose monitoring and AID system data will also be reviewed throughout the study.

The target is 12 evaluable participants, with a maximum of 14 participants allowed to account for early withdrawals before an evaluable post-baseline assessment. The study includes a screening period, approximately 24 weeks of treatment and follow-up assessments through week 30.

Safety assessments will include treatment-emergent adverse events, gastrointestinal symptoms, hypoglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis, as well as monitoring of tolerability during dose escalation. An independent Data and Safety Monitoring Committee is planned in accordance with the protocol.

The trial will be conducted at two Spanish hospital centers: Hospital Universitario Ramón y Cajal and Hospital Universitari i Politècnic La Fe. The study is exploratory and mechanistic; it is intended to characterize pharmacodynamic effects, estimate within-subject changes and inform the design of future confirmatory studies, rather than establish definitive clinical efficacy.
lead_sponsor: Fundacion para la Investigacion Biomedica del Hospital Universitario Ramon y Cajal
primary_outcomes: To characterize the dose-dependent effect of tirzepatide (2.5-15 mg) on gastric emptying (GE) in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) and overweight/obesity, assessed as the within-subject change from baseline using gastric emptying scintigraphy (GES).
title: Study to Evaluate the Dose-Dependent Effect of Tirzepatide on Gastric Emptying in Adult Patients With Type 1 Diabetes

brief_summary: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is the most common preventable cause of death after major abdominal and pelvic cancer surgery, and over one-third of events occur after discharge. Aim 1 uses interviews, focus groups, and surveys with patients, clinicians, and health system stakeholders to identify barriers and facilitators to implementing a post-discharge VTE chemoprophylaxis quality improvement project. Aim 2 uses retrospective hospital- and population-level data and coincidence analysis to identify hospital performance phenotypes and develop targeted implementation strategies. Findings will inform a separately registered stepped-wedge implementation trial (Aim 3).
